definition_zh: 批准；认可；制裁；批准（动词）
definition_en: official approval or permission; a penalty imposed to force obedience; to approve or authorize officially
core_image: 一份盖了官印的文件，既给出许可也带有强制力
scene: 政府批准了这项新计划。The government sanctioned the new plan.
sceneCN: 这里 sanction 是「批准」（第 3 个义项）；句意：政府批准了这项新计划。

senses.title: Official approval
senses.definition: official permission or approval for an action
senses.definitionCN: 对某项行动的官方许可或认可
senses.example: The plan needs the sanction of the council.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划需要议会批准。
senses.why: The core sense is the authority that makes an act valid.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是使行为有效的权威认可。

senses.title: A penalty
senses.definition: a punishment imposed, often by one country on another, to force obedience
senses.definitionCN: 常指一国对另一国施加、迫使其服从的惩罚措施
senses.example: The country faces tough economic sanctions.
senses.exampleCN: 该国面临严厉的经济制裁。
senses.why: Authority can also punish those who break the rule.
senses.whyCN: 权威也能惩罚违反规则者。

senses.title: To approve officially
senses.definition: to give official approval or permission for something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事给予官方批准或许可
senses.example: The board sanctioned the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会批准了预算。
senses.why: The verb applies the approval sense to an object.
senses.whyCN: 动词义把「批准」这一义项用于具体对象。

intro.en: Sanction comes from Latin sanctio, a decree, from sancire, to make sacred or ratify.
intro.cn: sanction 来自拉丁语 sanctio（法令），源头 sancire 意为使神圣或批准。

items.en: Sancire means to make sacred or confirm.
items.cn: sancire 意为使神圣或确认。

items.en: Sanctio names a binding decree.
items.cn: sanctio 指具有约束力的法令。

items.en: The word passes through legal French.
items.cn: 该词经由法律法语传入。

items.en: English sanction means a confirming law.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语 sanction 指确认性法律。

items.en: The word also means a punitive measure.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词也指惩罚性措施。

note.en: Sanction can mean approval or penalty; section is just a part.
note.cn: sanction 既可指批准也可指制裁，section 只是部分。

entries.definition: one part of something larger
a place where trains stop
a small group within a larger one
official agreement to something
a punishment for breaking a rule
an official ban on trade

normalIntro.en: Sanction is one word with two opposite faces: permission and punishment.
normalIntro.cn: sanction 一词两面：既是许可，也是惩罚。

normal.en: The minister sanctioned the export deal.
normal.cn: 部长批准了这笔出口交易。

normal.en: The UN imposed sanctions on the regime.
normal.cn: 联合国对该政权实施了制裁。

normal.en: He acted without official sanction.
normal.cn: 他未经官方批准就行动了。

normal.en: The sanctions were lifted last year.
normal.cn: 制裁去年被解除了。

normal.en: The school sanctioned the new club.
normal.cn: 学校批准了这个新社团。

abstract.en: Picture a wax seal that both permits and punishes.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚既授权又惩戒的蜡封。

abstract.en: Imagine a gate opened by a signature.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇由签名打开的闸门。

abstract.en: Think of a heavy fine as the price of breaking rules.
abstract.cn: 把高额罚款想成违规的代价。

examples.en: The project cannot start without official sanction.
examples.cn: 这个项目未经官方批准不能启动。

examples.en: New sanctions target the country's banks.
examples.cn: 新的制裁针对该国的银行。

examples.en: The committee sanctioned the use of the hall.
examples.cn: 委员会批准使用大厅。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: sanction 源于拉丁语 sancire（使神圣、批准），同族词有 sacred 与 saint，记住「由权威定下并强制执行」。

root: sanction 源自拉丁语 sanctio（法令），来自 sancire（使神圣、批准），与 saint、sacred 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Sanction means official approval, a punitive measure, or to approve officially.
sensesIntro.cn: sanction 指官方批准、惩罚性制裁，或正式批准某事的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an official seal that both permits and punishes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚既授权又惩戒的官印。

branches.en: The base sense is official approval.
branches.cn: 基础义是官方批准。

branches.en: The same authority imposes penalties.
branches.cn: 同一权威施加惩罚。

branches.en: The verb turns approval into an action.
branches.cn: 动词义把批准变成动作。

branches.en: Approval and authorizing describe one official act.
branches.cn: 批准与授权描述同一个官方行为。

branches.en: Powers that sanction deals can also sanction states.
branches.cn: 能批准交易的力量也能制裁国家。

intro.en: Sanction belongs to the sanct- family of words about what is sacred or binding.
intro.cn: sanction 属于 sanct- 词族，表示神圣或有约束力的事物。

latinIntro.en: Latin sancire, sanctio, and sanctus form the root family of sanction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sancire、sanctio 与 sanctus 构成 sanction 的词根家族。

items.example: They gave their sanction to the plan.

items.meaning: approved or subjected to a penalty
items.exampleCN: 这次罢工获得官方批准。

items.meaning: the act of approving or penalizing
items.exampleCN: 批准此类出口颇具争议。
他们举行了一次未经批准的会议。

items.example: They defended the sanctity of life.
items.exampleCN: 他们捍卫生命的神圣性。

items.example: The birds found sanctuary in the woods.
items.exampleCN: 鸟儿在树林里找到了庇护。

items.example: The ritual was meant to sanctify the ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个仪式意在使土地神圣。

latinEntries.example: Sancire is the root of sanction.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sancire 是 sanction 的词根。
sanctus 是 saint 的前身。

definition_zh: 圣所；至圣所；避难所；野生动物保护区；庇护地位
definition_en: the holiest part of a religious building, or a place where a person, animal or community is protected from harm
core_image: 一道厚重的门帘后面是空无一物的内室，门外的人只能停在台阶上
scene: 战火逼近时，修道院的大门向逃难的人敞开。The old abbey became a sanctuary for families who had lost their homes.
sceneCN: 这里 sanctuary 指「使人免受伤害的庇护之所」（第 2 个义项：避难所）；句意为那座古老修道院成了失去家园的家庭的避难所。图中可辨识物件：修道院大门、门帘、台阶、逃难者的行囊。

senses.title: The holiest inner room
senses.definition: the most sacred room of a temple or church, often separated by a screen or curtain
senses.definitionCN: 神庙或教堂中最神圣的房间，常以屏风或门帘隔开
senses.example: Only the high priest entered the inner sanctuary once a year.
senses.exampleCN: 只有大祭司每年进入至圣所一次。
senses.why: the word comes from the Latin for 'holy place', so its first sense is the room set apart as most holy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语「神圣之地」，因此第一个义项就是被分别出来、最为神圣的房间。

senses.title: A place of refuge
senses.definition: a place where a person in danger can stay safe from pursuit or violence
senses.definitionCN: 身处危险者可在此免受追捕或暴力侵害的地方
senses.example: The villagers gave the refugees sanctuary for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 村民让难民在那里避难过冬。
senses.why: a holy place was physically inviolable, so protection from harm became the word's everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 神圣之地在实体上不可侵犯，因此「免受伤害」成为这个词的日常义。

senses.title: A protected area for wildlife
senses.definition: an area where hunting and development are restricted so that animals can breed
senses.definitionCN: 限制狩猎与开发、使动物得以繁殖的区域
senses.example: The marsh was declared a sanctuary for nesting birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沼泽被宣布为筑巢鸟类的保护区。
senses.why: the idea of a space where harm is forbidden transfers easily from people to animals.
senses.whyCN: 「禁止伤害」的空间这一观念，从人身上转到动物身上十分自然。

senses.title: The medieval right of sanctuary
senses.definition: the legal privilege by which a fugitive who reached a church could not be seized for a set period
senses.definitionCN: 逃犯抵达教堂后在一定期限内不得被逮捕的法律特权
senses.example: He claimed the right of sanctuary and stayed forty days.
senses.exampleCN: 他援引教堂庇护权，留了四十天。
senses.why: the church's immunity was a real legal rule, so the word named a procedure, not only a feeling of safety.
senses.whyCN: 教会的不可侵犯性曾是真实的法律规则，因此这个词指一套程序，而不只是一种安全感。

senses.title: A quiet place for the mind
senses.definition: a place or activity that gives relief from pressure and noise
senses.definitionCN: 使人从压力与喧闹中获得缓解的地方或活动
senses.example: The garden shed is his sanctuary after a long shift.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间轮班之后，那间园艺小屋是他的避难所。
senses.why: refuge need not be physical; the word follows the feeling of being shielded.
senses.whyCN: 庇护不必是实体的；这个词跟着「被遮蔽」的感受走。

senses.title: A city that shields migrants
senses.definition: a city that limits cooperation with immigration enforcement and offers services to undocumented residents
senses.definitionCN: 限制与移民执法合作、并向无证居民提供服务的城市
senses.example: The city declared itself a sanctuary and refused to hold detainees for federal agents.
senses.exampleCN: 该市宣布自己是庇护城市，拒绝为联邦人员关押被拘者。
senses.why: modern politics reused the old legal word for a municipal policy of non-cooperation.
senses.whyCN: 现代政治把这一古老法律词重新用于市政层面的不合作政策。

senses.title: Inviolable protection
senses.definition: the state of being protected from interference by authorities or outsiders
senses.definitionCN: 免受当局或外来者干预的保护状态
senses.example: The archive claims sanctuary from political pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 该档案馆声称享有免受政治压力干预的庇护。
senses.why: when the place is abstract, the word names the immunity itself rather than a building.
senses.whyCN: 当地点变得抽象时，这个词指豁免本身，而非某座建筑。

senses.title: The altar area of a church
senses.definition: in church architecture, the area around the altar, often raised and separated from the nave
senses.definitionCN: 教堂建筑中祭坛周围、常被抬高并与中殿隔开的区域
senses.example: The sanctuary step marks where the choir stalls begin.
senses.exampleCN: 圣坛区的台阶标出唱诗席开始的位置。
senses.why: builders needed a precise word for the holiest zone of the floor plan, so the religious term became a measuring term.
senses.whyCN: 建造者需要一个精确的词来指平面图上的至圣区域，于是宗教词变成量度用词。

intro.en: Sanctuary comes from the Latin noun for a holy place, built on the verb that made things sacred. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sanctuary 来自拉丁语中表示「神圣之地」的名词，其基础是使事物成为神圣的动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sacer meant sacred or dedicated to a god, and it stood at the centre of Roman religious vocabulary.
items.cn: sacer 意为神圣的、献给神的，处于罗马宗教词汇的核心。

items.en: Sancire meant to make sacred, to ratify or to forbid violation; a law was 'sanctioned' by being made untouchable.
items.cn: sancire 意为使神圣、批准或禁止侵犯；一条法律因不可触犯而获得「批准」。

items.en: The participle sanctus described what had been made holy, and it became the everyday word for a saint.
items.cn: 分词 sanctus 描述已被视为神圣之物，后来成为指「圣人」的日常词。

items.en: Sanctuarium named the place where holy things were kept, and in Christian use the holiest part of a church.
items.cn: sanctuarium 指存放圣物之处，在基督教用法中指教堂中最神圣的部分。

items.en: Old French saintuaire carried the word into English, where it widened from the holy room to any place of shelter.
items.cn: 古法语 saintuaire 把这个词带入英语，其义从神圣房间扩展到任何庇护之处。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link between sacer and sancire is widely accepted in outline but the exact derivation and the pre-Latin ancestry of either word are not settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：sacer 与 sancire 之间的联系在轮廓上被广泛接受，但确切派生关系与两词在拉丁语之前的谱系都尚无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same holiness root or easily confused with refuge terms; group two holds other words for protection.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「神圣」词根或容易与避难类词混淆的词；第二组是其他表示保护的词。

entries.definition: The state of being holy; it is an abstract quality, while sanctuary is a place or a protected condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指神圣的状态，是抽象属性；而 sanctuary 指地点或受保护的状态。

entries.definition: To make something holy or set it apart for sacred use; the verb acts, the noun names the result.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物神圣或分别为圣；动词表示动作，名词表示结果。

entries.definition: Pretending to be morally superior; the word mocks a show of holiness rather than naming a place.
entries.definitionCN: 假装道德高人一等；这个词嘲讽神圣的姿态，而非指地点。

entries.definition: A private or inviolable room, from the Latin for 'holy thing'; it is smaller and more personal than a sanctuary.
entries.definitionCN: 私密或不可侵犯的房间，来自拉丁语「神圣之物」；比 sanctuary 更小、更私人。

entries.definition: A place or state of safety from danger; it is the plain word, while sanctuary adds a sacred or legal flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 脱离危险的处所或状态；这是朴素说法，sanctuary 则带神圣或法律色彩。

entries.definition: Protection granted by a state to a foreigner, or an old word for an institution for the mentally ill.
entries.definitionCN: 国家给予外国人的保护，也旧指精神病院。

entries.definition: An area protected for wildlife or landscape; it is a conservation term without religious overtones.
entries.definitionCN: 为野生动物或景观保护的区域；是保育术语，无宗教意味。

entries.definition: A structure or state giving cover from weather or attack; it makes no claim of inviolability.
entries.definitionCN: 提供遮风避雨或防护的结构或状态，不含不可侵犯之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real holiness root, the real legal history and the real conservation use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「神圣」词根、真实的法律史与真实的保育用法。

normal.en: The root means 'made sacred', so the place is first untouchable and only then comforting.
normal.cn: 词根意为「被祝圣」，因此这地方先是不可侵犯，然后才令人安心。

normal.en: The family runs sanctuary, sanctify, sanctity, sanctification, sanctimonious.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sanctuary、sanctify、sanctity、sanctification、sanctimonious。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: wildlife sanctuary, sanctuary city, right of sanctuary.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：野生动物保护区、庇护城市、教堂庇护权。

normal.en: A church's holiest room and a marsh for nesting birds are both places where harm is forbidden.
normal.cn: 教堂的至圣所与鸟类的筑巢沼泽，都是禁止伤害的地方。

normal.en: The same word in a floor plan names the raised area around the altar.
normal.cn: 在平面图上，同一个词指祭坛周围被抬高的区域。

abstract.en: Picture a line on the floor that no pursuer is allowed to cross.
abstract.cn: 想象地上画着一条线，追捕者不被允许跨过。

abstract.en: Picture a room with no furniture, only a curtain and a step.
abstract.cn: 想象一间没有家具的房间，只有一道门帘与一级台阶。

abstract.en: Picture a garden shed that becomes the smallest possible country.
abstract.cn: 想象一间园艺小屋成了最小的国度。

examples.en: The hermit built a sanctuary of stone and turf on the island.
examples.cn: 隐修士在岛上用石头与草皮建了一处圣所。

examples.en: The forest is a sanctuary for the last wild herd.
examples.cn: 这片森林是最后一群野生兽群的保护区。

examples.en: She found sanctuary in the reading room during the strike.
examples.cn: 罢工期间，她在阅览室里找到了安宁。

dict_mnemonic.text: sanct（神圣）+ uary（场所）→ 神圣不可侵犯之处 → 圣所、避难所

root: 拉丁 sanctuarium「存放圣物之处」来自 sanctus「神圣的」，其动词 sancire 意为「使神圣、批准、禁止侵犯」；英语 sanctuary。sacer 与 sancire 的确切派生关系不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one boundary: a room marked off as untouchable becomes a refuge, then a conservation area, a legal privilege, a mental shelter, a city policy, a form of immunity and finally a point on a floor plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条界线展开：被划为不可侵犯的房间成为避难所，再成为保护区、法律特权、心灵庇护、城市政策、豁免形式，最后成为平面图上的一点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a threshold that danger is not allowed to cross.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道危险不得越过的门槛。

branches.en: THE ROOM: the holiest inner space and the altar area are the same sacred zone at different scales.
branches.cn: 房间：至圣所与圣坛区，是同一神圣区域的两个尺度。

branches.en: REFUGE: a physical shelter for the body and a quiet place for the mind follow the same feeling of being shielded.
branches.cn: 庇护：身体的庇护所与心灵的安静处，跟随同一种被遮蔽的感受。

branches.en: PROTECTED LAND: the untouchable zone is applied to animals and their breeding grounds.
branches.cn: 受保护的土地：不可侵犯的区域被用于动物及其繁殖地。

branches.en: IMMUNITY: the medieval right and the modern claim both name protection from seizure or pressure.
branches.cn: 豁免：中世纪的庇护权与现代的豁免主张，都指免受抓捕或压力。

branches.en: POLICY: a city borrows the old word for a modern rule about migrants.
branches.cn: 政策：一座城市借这个旧词表达现代移民规则。

intro.en: Sanctuary is built from a Latin root for 'sacred' plus a suffix for a place, and that root also builds a whole family of English words.
intro.cn: sanctuary 由拉丁语「神圣」词根加表示场所的后缀构成，这个词根还构成一整族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sacer, sancire and sanctus produced sanctuarium; English later formed sanctify, sanctity and sanctimonious from the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sacer、sancire 与 sanctus 产生 sanctuarium；英语后来用同一词干构成 sanctify、sanctity 与 sanctimonious。

items.example: Sacer marked what belonged to the gods.
items.exampleCN: sacer 标记属于神明之物。

items.structure: sancire, sanxi, sanctum (Latin verb, fourth conjugation)
items.meaning: to make sacred, ratify, forbid violation
items.example: The law was sancire before it was written.
items.exampleCN: 这条法律在被写下之前就已受批准。

items.structure: sanctus, sancta, sanctum (Latin participle used as adjective)
items.example: Sanctus named a person as well as a place.
items.exampleCN: 这个词既指人，也指地方。
仪式使寻常物件变得神圣。

items.example: The sanctity of the site is legally protected.
items.exampleCN: 该地的神圣性受法律保护。
他那假虔诚的腔调骗不了任何人。

definition_zh: 环境卫生；排污设施；卫生设备
definition_en: the systems and services that remove sewage and waste and keep public places clean and healthy
core_image: 地下管道把污水送走，地面保持干净
scene: 市政工人正在疏通下水管道，避免污水漫上街道。City workers were clearing the sewers to protect sanitation in the district.
sceneCN: 这里 sanitation 是「环境卫生」（第 2 个义项：一个地方干净、供水安全、废物不堆积的状态）；句意：市政工人疏通下水管道，以维护这一区域的环境卫生。

derivatives.zh: sanitation 的词干 sanit- 加形容词后缀 -ary 构成，义为「卫生的；清洁的」
同一词干加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「消毒；使清洁卫生」
同一词干加表示人的后缀 -ian 构成，义为「公共卫生工作者；卫生学家」

senses.title: Sewage and waste systems
senses.definition: the physical systems, such as sewers, drains, and treatment plants, that carry sewage and waste away
senses.definitionCN: 下水道、排水管、处理厂等把污水和废物运走的实体系统
senses.example: The village finally gained proper sanitation last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子去年终于有了像样的排污设施。
senses.why: Latin sanitas means health, and the suffix -ation names the process of making something healthy, so the noun first names the works that remove what threatens health.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sanitas 意为健康，后缀 -ation 表示使……的过程，因此这个词最初指清除健康威胁的工程设施。

senses.title: Clean and healthy conditions
senses.definition: the state of a place being clean, with safe water and no accumulating waste
senses.definitionCN: 一个地方干净、供水安全、废物不堆积的状态
senses.example: Poor sanitation in the camp allowed disease to spread.
senses.exampleCN: 营地里环境卫生差，疾病得以传播。
senses.why: Once the works exist, the word also names the condition they produce.
senses.whyCN: 设施建成之后，这个词也用来指这些设施带来的清洁状态。

senses.title: Public sanitation services
senses.definition: the collection, treatment, and inspection services that a community provides to keep public spaces healthy
senses.definitionCN: 社区为保持公共空间卫生而提供的收集、处理与检查服务
senses.example: The council spends a large share of its budget on sanitation.
senses.exampleCN: 市政会把很大一部分预算花在公共环卫服务上。
senses.why: Health protection becomes an organized public duty, not only a private habit.
senses.whyCN: 健康保护由此成为有组织的公共职责，而不只是私人习惯。

senses.title: Safe food handling
senses.definition: the cleaning and safe handling of food and equipment in kitchens and food businesses
senses.definitionCN: 厨房与食品企业中食物和设备的清洁与安全处理
senses.example: Food sanitation inspectors closed the dirty restaurant.
senses.exampleCN: 食品卫生检查员关停了那家不洁餐馆。
senses.why: The same health logic narrows to the kitchen, where contamination reaches people directly.
senses.whyCN: 同样的健康逻辑收窄到厨房，因为污染在那里直接进入人体。

senses.title: Sanitary science
senses.definition: the study of the conditions and methods that protect public health
senses.definitionCN: 研究保护公共卫生的条件与方法的学科
senses.example: He studied sanitation and water engineering at university.
senses.exampleCN: 他在大学学习卫生学与水利工程。
senses.why: The practical works grew into a body of knowledge with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 实务工程逐渐长成一门有自己名称的知识体系。

senses.title: Ecological sanitation
senses.definition: waste systems that recover nutrients and water instead of polluting the environment
senses.definitionCN: 回收养分和水、不污染环境的废物处理系统
senses.example: Ecological sanitation turns human waste into safe fertilizer.
senses.exampleCN: 生态卫生设施把人的排泄物变成安全的肥料。
senses.why: New environmental priorities add a branch that treats waste as a resource.
senses.whyCN: 新的环境诉求增加了一个把废物视为资源的分支。

senses.title: Emergency sanitation
senses.definition: temporary toilets and waste systems provided after disasters or in refugee camps
senses.definitionCN: 灾害之后或难民营中提供的临时厕所与废物处理系统
senses.example: Aid groups rushed emergency sanitation to the flood zone.
senses.exampleCN: 救援组织把应急环卫设施紧急送往洪灾区。
senses.why: When normal systems collapse, the same need produces a temporary, crisis version.
senses.whyCN: 当常规系统瘫痪时，同样的需求催生出临时的危机版本。

intro.en: Sanitation is built on Latin sanitas, health, from sanus, healthy, with the English action suffix -ation added in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: sanitation 建于拉丁语 sanitas（健康）之上，其词根 sanus 意为健康的，十九世纪再加英语后缀 -ation 构成。

items.en: Sanus means healthy or sound.
items.cn: sanus 意为健康的、健全的。

items.en: Sanitas names health or soundness of body.
items.cn: sanitas 指健康或身体的健全。

items.en: Sanare means to heal or to make healthy.
items.cn: sanare 意为治愈或使健康。

items.en: English coins sanitation from the stem sanit- plus -ation for the work of making places sanitary.
items.cn: 英语用 sanit- 词干加 -ation 造出 sanitation，指使场所卫生的工作。

items.en: Reformers linked dirty water to cholera and demanded public sanitation.
items.cn: 改革者把污水与霍乱联系起来，要求建设公共环卫设施。

items.en: Modern sanitation spans sewers, water treatment, and waste recycling.
items.cn: 现代 sanitation 涵盖下水道、水处理与废物回收。

note.en: Sanitation is the Latin health word applied to public works, close to sanitary and sanitize and to the vocabulary of sewage and hygiene.
note.cn: sanitation 是拉丁语「健康」一词用于公共工程的产物，与 sanitary、sanitize 以及 sewage、hygiene 等词汇相邻。

entries.definition: clean and designed to protect health
to clean something and kill germs on it
a specialist in public health and sanitation
entries.definitionCN: 公共卫生工作者；卫生学家

entries.definition: the practices that keep people clean and healthy
waste water and refuse carried away by sewers
the network of sewers and drains

normalIntro.en: Sanitation is health made public: pipes, drains, and services that keep a whole place clean.
normalIntro.cn: sanitation 是被公共化的健康：管道、排水与服务共同维持一个地方的清洁。

normal.en: Basic sanitation means safe toilets and clean water for everyone.
normal.cn: 基本卫生设施意味着人人有安全厕所和清洁饮水。

normal.en: A sanitation system carries waste away from homes.
normal.cn: 排污系统把废物从住宅运走。

normal.en: Sanitation workers collect rubbish and maintain drains.
normal.cn: 环卫工人收集垃圾并维护排水设施。

normal.en: The adjective sanitary describes clean, health-safe conditions.
normal.cn: 形容词 sanitary 描述清洁、对健康无害的条件。

normal.en: Compare hygiene: hygiene is the habit, sanitation is the system.
normal.cn: 对比 hygiene：hygiene 是习惯，sanitation 是设施与系统。

abstract.en: Picture a sewer pipe running under a clean street.
abstract.cn: 想象一条下水管道在干净街道的地下延伸。

abstract.en: Imagine a tap of clear water beside a row of covered drains.
abstract.cn: 想象一排加盖的排水沟旁接着一管清水。

abstract.en: Think of a textbook on pipes and pumps that protects a city.
abstract.cn: 想象一本讲管道与泵、守护整座城市的教科书。

examples.en: The town built a modern sanitation network after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，小镇建起了现代化的排污网络。

examples.en: Poor sanitation in the camp caused an outbreak of dysentery.
examples.cn: 营地里环境卫生差，引发了痢疾暴发。

examples.en: Clean water and sanitation are basic public health needs.
examples.cn: 清洁饮水与环境卫生是基本的公共卫生需求。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三泥太深」——污水淤泥积得太深，就必须修设施治理；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 sanus（健康的）→ sanitas（健康）→ 词干 sanit- 加 -ation → 英语 sanitation，核心义「让环境保持健康」。

sensesIntro.en: Sanitation starts from the physical works that remove waste, then names the clean condition they produce and the public services that run them, before branching into food, science, ecology, and emergency relief.
sensesIntro.cn: sanitation 从运走废物的实体设施出发，继而指设施带来的清洁状态与运营这些设施的公共服务，再分出食品、学科、生态与应急救援等分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an underground pipe carrying waste away while the street stays clean.
core.cn: 核心意象：地下管道把污水送走，地面保持干净。

branches.en: The physical waste systems are the founding branch.
branches.cn: 实体排污设施是最初的分支。

branches.en: The clean condition of a place is the state branch.
branches.cn: 场所的清洁状态是状态分支。

branches.en: Public services and food inspection turn the system into daily administration.
branches.cn: 公共服务与食品检查把系统变成日常管理。

branches.en: Sanitary science is the academic branch.
branches.cn: 卫生学是学术分支。

branches.en: Ecology and emergencies push the system toward resources and crisis response.
branches.cn: 生态与紧急状况把系统推向资源回收与危机应对。

intro.en: Sanitation joins the Latin health stem sanit- to the action suffix -ation, and the same stem yields sanitary, sanitize, and sanitarian.
intro.cn: sanitation 由拉丁语健康词干 sanit- 与表示行为的名词后缀 -ation 组合而成，同一词干还产出 sanitary、sanitize 与 sanitarian。

latinIntro.en: Latin sanus means healthy, sanitas means health, and sanare means to heal; all three feed the English sanit- family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sanus 意为健康的，sanitas 意为健康，sanare 意为治愈；三者共同滋养英语的 sanit- 词族。

items.example: Sanus is the adjective behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: sanus 是整个词族背后的形容词。

items.example: Sanitas gives English the stem sanit-.
items.exampleCN: sanitas 为英语提供 sanit- 词干。

items.example: Sanare adds the idea of restoring health.
items.exampleCN: sanare 增添了恢复健康的意思。

items.example: The stem sanit- appears in sanitary and sanitation.
items.exampleCN: 词干 sanit- 出现在 sanitary 与 sanitation 中。

items.example: The suffix -ation turns the stem into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 把词干变成表示行为的名词。

items.example: Sanitation names the organized work of keeping places healthy.
items.exampleCN: sanitation 指使场所保持卫生的有组织工作。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms the adjective sanitary.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ary 构成形容词 sanitary。
卫生的条件能预防疾病。

items.example: Staff sanitize the tables after every meal.
items.exampleCN: 员工每餐后给桌子消毒。

items.example: The prefix in- reverses sanitary into insanitary.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 sanitary 反义为 insanitary。

items.example: A sanitarian inspects water and waste systems.
items.exampleCN: 卫生工作者检查供水与废物系统。

definition_zh: 卫星；人造卫星；卫星城；附属国
definition_en: a natural body orbiting a planet; a man-made object placed in orbit; a place or state dependent on a larger one
core_image: 一个小天体或装置围绕更大的主体不停旋转
scene: 这颗卫星正绕地球运行。The satellite is orbiting the Earth.
sceneCN: 这里 satellite 是「人造卫星」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这颗卫星正绕地球运行。

senses.title: A natural moon
senses.definition: a natural body that orbits a planet
senses.definitionCN: 围绕行星运行的天体
senses.example: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite.
senses.exampleCN: 月球是地球唯一的天然卫星。
senses.why: The base sense is a smaller body circling a larger one.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是围绕更大天体运行的小天体。

senses.title: A man-made orbiter
senses.definition: a machine sent into orbit around the Earth or another body
senses.definitionCN: 被送入地球或其他天体轨道的装置
senses.example: The satellite sends weather data every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗卫星每小时传送一次气象数据。
senses.why: Technology copies the motion of a natural moon.
senses.whyCN: 技术复制了天然卫星的运行方式。

senses.title: A dependent place
senses.definition: a town or country that depends on a larger one nearby
senses.definitionCN: 依附于附近更大城镇或国家的城镇或国家
senses.example: The factory town became a satellite of the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这座工厂城镇成了首都的卫星城。
senses.why: The image of circling around a centre extends to politics and cities.
senses.whyCN: 围绕中心的意象延伸到政治与城市。

intro.en: Satellite comes from Latin satelles, a guard or attendant.
intro.cn: satellite 来自拉丁语 satelles（卫兵、随从）。

items.en: Satelles means an attendant or guard.
items.cn: satelles 意为随从或卫兵。

items.en: The word enters French as satellite.
items.cn: 该词以 satellite 形式进入法语。

items.en: English uses satellite for a follower.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语用 satellite 指追随者。

items.en: The word comes to mean a moon.
items.cn: 天文学中该词转为指卫星。

items.en: After Sputnik it means a man-made orbiter.
items.cn: 斯普特尼克之后指人造卫星。

note.en: A satellite orbits a body; a settle is a wooden bench.
note.cn: satellite 是绕行天体，settle 则是木长凳。

entries.definition: to come to rest or agree
humour that mocks faults
to greet with respect
a natural body orbiting a planet
a vehicle designed for space
a craft that circles a body

normalIntro.en: Satellite covers natural moons, space machines, and dependent places.
normalIntro.cn: satellite 涵盖天然卫星、航天器与附属城镇。

normal.en: The Moon is a natural satellite.
normal.cn: 月球是一颗天然卫星。

normal.en: They launched a weather satellite.
normal.cn: 他们发射了一颗气象卫星。

normal.en: We watched the match on satellite television.
normal.cn: 我们通过卫星电视看了比赛。

normal.en: The satellite dish was on the roof.
normal.cn: 卫星天线装在屋顶上。

normal.en: The small town is a satellite of the city.
normal.cn: 这个小镇是那座城市的卫星城。

abstract.en: Picture a small light circling a large lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏小灯绕着一盏大灯转。

abstract.en: Imagine a guard always walking beside a king.
abstract.cn: 想象一名卫兵始终走在国王身旁。

abstract.en: Think of a town whose life depends on a bigger city.
abstract.cn: 想象一座依赖大城市的城镇。

examples.en: Jupiter has more than ninety known satellites.
examples.cn: 木星有九十多颗已知卫星。

examples.en: The satellite was placed in a low orbit.
examples.cn: 这颗卫星被送入低轨道。

examples.en: Several satellite towns surround the capital.
examples.cn: 首都周围有几座卫星城。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁随从
dict_mnemonic.text: satellite 原意是「随从、卫兵」，随从总跟着主人，正如卫星总绕着行星。

root: satellite 来自拉丁语 satelles（卫兵、随从），由「跟随者」引申为绕行天体与人造卫星。

sensesIntro.en: Satellite is a natural moon, a man-made orbiter, or a dependent place.
sensesIntro.cn: satellite 指天然卫星、人造卫星，或依附性的城镇与国家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smaller body circling a larger one.
core.cn: 核心意象：小一圈的物体围绕更大的主体。

branches.en: The base sense is a natural body in orbit.
branches.cn: 基础义是轨道上的天然天体。

branches.en: Technology copies the moon's motion.
branches.cn: 技术复制了卫星的运行方式。

branches.en: Dependence extends the image to places.
branches.cn: 依附关系把意象延伸到地方。

branches.en: Natural moons and machines both orbit planets.
branches.cn: 天然卫星与机器都绕行星运行。

branches.en: Both are controlled or supported by a centre.
branches.cn: 两者都受中心控制或支持。

intro.en: Satellite combines with nouns to name space technology and dependent places.
intro.cn: satellite 与名词组合，指太空技术与依附性地方。

latinIntro.en: Latin satelles and its genitive satellitis are the source of satellite.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 satelles 及其属格 satellitis 是 satellite 的源头。

items.meaning: an orbiting body or a dependent place

items.meaning: a dish antenna for satellite signals

救援人员携带了卫星电话。

items.meaning: a town dependent on a nearby city

items.meaning: a country controlled by a stronger one

items.exampleCN: 这个说法描述一个附庸国。

latinEntries.example: Satelles is the root of satellite.

latinEntries.example: Satellitis shows the stem used in derivatives.
latinEntries.exampleCN: satellitis 展示了派生词使用的词干。

definition_en: a feeling of pleasure when a need or hope is met; the fulfilment of a demand or obligation; compensation for a wrong
core_image: 一个空杯子被倒满，心里也随之安稳
scene: 她对考试结果很满意。She felt great satisfaction with her exam results.
sceneCN: 这里 satisfaction 是「满意、满足」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她对考试结果很满意。

forms.label: 复数（指具体的满足或补偿）

senses.title: Contentment
senses.definition: a feeling of pleasure when a need or hope is met
senses.definitionCN: 需要或希望得到满足时的愉快感受
senses.example: She smiled with satisfaction.
senses.exampleCN: 她满意地笑了。
senses.why: The core sense is the good feeling of having enough.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是「足够」带来的良好感受。

senses.title: Fulfilment of a claim
senses.definition: the act of fulfilling a demand, duty, or debt
senses.definitionCN: 满足要求、履行职责或清偿债务的行为
senses.example: The company worked for the satisfaction of all claims.
senses.exampleCN: 公司努力清偿所有索赔。
senses.why: The feeling of enough extends to settling what is owed.
senses.whyCN: 「足够」的感受延伸到结清所欠之物。

senses.title: Compensation
senses.definition: something given to make up for a wrong or injury
senses.definitionCN: 为弥补过错或伤害而给予的东西
senses.example: He demanded satisfaction for the insult.
senses.exampleCN: 他要求为受辱获得补偿。
senses.why: An old legal sense treats a wrong as a debt to be paid.
senses.whyCN: 古老的法律义把过错视为需要偿还的债。

intro.en: Satisfaction comes from Latin satisfactio, from satis enough and facere to make.
intro.cn: satisfaction 来自拉丁语 satisfactio，由 satis（足够）与 facere（做）构成。

items.en: Satis means enough.
items.cn: satis 意为足够。

items.en: Facere means to make or do.
items.cn: facere 意为做或制造。

items.en: Satisfactio means making amends.
items.cn: satisfactio 意为作出补偿。

items.en: The word enters French legal use.
items.cn: 该词进入法语法律用语。

items.en: It names both contentment and compensation.
items.cn: 现代英语中它兼指满意与补偿。

note.en: Satisfaction is the feeling of enough; saturation means being full to the limit.
note.cn: satisfaction 是满足感，saturation 则是达到饱和。

entries.definition: the state of being completely full
approval or a penalty
a feeling of not being pleased
quiet happiness with what one has
the achievement of a need or aim
pleasure from satisfying a desire

normalIntro.en: Satisfaction is what you feel when something is finally enough.
normalIntro.cn: satisfaction 就是事情终于「足够」时的感受。

normal.en: She looked at the finished work with satisfaction.
normal.cn: 她满意地看着完成的作品。

normal.en: Customer satisfaction has risen this year.
normal.cn: 今年顾客满意度上升了。

normal.en: The matter was settled to everyone's satisfaction.
normal.cn: 这件事以人人满意的方式解决了。

normal.en: He gets great satisfaction from teaching.
normal.cn: 他从教学中获得极大满足。

normal.en: The court demanded satisfaction of the debt.
normal.cn: 法院要求清偿这笔债务。

abstract.en: Picture an empty cup filled to the brim.
abstract.cn: 想象一个空杯被倒到杯沿。

abstract.en: Imagine a debt crossed out at last.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔债务终于被划掉。

abstract.en: Think of a wrong balanced by a fair payment.
abstract.cn: 把过错想成由公平偿付来平衡。

examples.en: He nodded in satisfaction at the result.
examples.cn: 他对结果满意地点了点头。

examples.en: The workers expressed satisfaction with the new rules.
examples.cn: 工人们对新规定表示满意。

examples.en: The injured party sought satisfaction in court.
examples.cn: 受害方在法庭上寻求补偿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup filled to the brim and set at rest.

branches.en: The base sense is the feeling of enough.
branches.cn: 基础义是「足够」带来的感受。

branches.en: Settling a claim brings contentment.

intro.en: Satisfaction belongs to the satisf- family built on satis and facere.

latinIntro.en: Latin satis, facere, and satisfacere explain satisfaction and satisfy.

senses.example: The test results were satisfactory.

senses.title: Meeting a standard

senses.title: Convincing

senses.definitionCN: 足以消除疑问或异议的
senses.example: He gave a satisfactory explanation for the delay.

senses.why: An answer is satisfactory when it settles the question.

intro.en: Satisfactory comes from Latin satisfacere, to satisfy, with the ending -ory.
intro.cn: satisfactory 来自拉丁语 satisfacere（使满足），加后缀 -ory。

items.en: Satis means enough.

items.en: Facere means to make or do.

items.en: Satisfacere means to satisfy.
items.cn: satisfacere 意为使满足。

items.en: The ending -orius means serving to do.

items.en: Satisfactory means good enough to accept.
items.cn: 现代英语中 satisfactory 意为好到可以接受。

note.en: Satisfactory describes a thing; satisfied describes a person's feeling.
note.cn: satisfactory 描述事物，satisfied 描述人的感受。

entries.definition: pleased because a need is met
giving a feeling of fulfilment
the feeling of contentment
good enough to be allowed
enough for a particular purpose
as much as is needed

normalIntro.en: Satisfactory means good enough, not necessarily excellent.
normalIntro.cn: satisfactory 意为够好，不一定出色。

normal.en: The repair work was satisfactory.
normal.cn: 维修工作令人满意。

normal.en: We need a satisfactory explanation.
normal.cn: 我们需要一个令人信服的解释。

normal.en: Her progress this term is satisfactory.
normal.cn: 她这学期的进步令人满意。

normal.en: The car is in satisfactory condition.
normal.cn: 这辆车状况良好。

normal.en: The answer was not satisfactory to the judge.
normal.cn: 这个答复未能让法官信服。

abstract.en: Picture a checklist with every box ticked.
abstract.cn: 想象一张所有方框都打勾的检查表。

abstract.en: Imagine a bridge passing its safety test.
abstract.cn: 想象一座通过安全测试的桥。

abstract.en: Think of a door that closes every doubt.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇关掉所有疑问的门。

examples.en: The quality of the goods was satisfactory.
examples.cn: 货物质量令人满意。

examples.en: They reached a satisfactory agreement.
examples.cn: 他们达成了令人满意的协议。

examples.en: The student's attendance was satisfactory.
examples.cn: 这名学生的出勤情况符合要求。

root: satisfactory 来自拉丁语 satisfacere（做到足够、使满足）加后缀 -ory，意为「能使人满意的」。

sensesIntro.en: Satisfactory means good enough, meeting a standard, or convincing.
sensesIntro.cn: satisfactory 表示够好、符合标准，或足以令人信服。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a checklist completed well enough to pass.

branches.en: The base sense is reaching an acceptable level.

branches.en: A standard defines what is acceptable.
branches.cn: 标准界定了何为可接受。

branches.en: A convincing answer settles the doubt.
branches.cn: 有说服力的答案消除疑问。

branches.en: Good enough often means meeting the rule.
branches.cn: 「够好」常常意味着符合规定。

latinIntro.en: Satisfactory joins satis, facere, and the Latin suffix -orius.

latinEntries.exampleCN: satis 是整个词族的锚点。

definition_zh: 使满意；满足；符合；使信服
definition_en: to make someone pleased or content; to fulfil a need or desire; to meet a requirement; to convince someone
core_image: 把对方需要的东西刚好给足
scene: 优质服务能满足顾客。Good service can satisfy customers.
sceneCN: 这里 satisfy 是「使满意」（第 1 个义项）；句意：优质服务能满足顾客。

senses.title: To please someone
senses.definition: to make someone feel pleased or content
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到愉快或满足
senses.example: The gift satisfied the child.
senses.exampleCN: 这份礼物让这个孩子很满意。
senses.why: The base sense is giving someone enough to be happy.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是给对方足够的东西使其高兴。

senses.title: To fulfil a need
senses.definition: to provide enough to meet a need, desire, or appetite
senses.definitionCN: 提供足以满足需要、欲望或胃口的东西
senses.example: A snack will satisfy your hunger.
senses.exampleCN: 一份点心就能让你不饿。
senses.why: A need is like an empty space that must be filled.
senses.whyCN: 需要就像一个必须被填满的空缺。

senses.title: To meet a requirement
senses.definition: to meet a rule, condition, or standard
senses.definitionCN: 达到规则、条件或标准
senses.example: The team must satisfy the entry rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍必须符合参赛规则。
senses.why: The idea of enough applies to formal conditions.
senses.whyCN: 「足够」的观念适用于正式条件。

senses.title: To convince
senses.definition: to give someone enough proof to remove doubt
senses.definitionCN: 提供足以消除疑问的证据
senses.example: The evidence satisfied the jury.
senses.exampleCN: 证据使陪审团信服了。
senses.why: Proof fills the space of doubt until nothing is left to question.
senses.whyCN: 证据填满疑问的空间，直到无可质疑。

intro.en: Satisfy comes from Latin satisfacere, from satis enough and facere to make.

items.en: Satis means enough.

items.en: Satisfy means to please, fulfil, or convince.

note.en: Satisfy means to give enough; satiate means to fill to excess.

entries.definition: to fill beyond what is wanted
to satisfy fully, often too much
giving a feeling of fulfilment
to make someone happy
to carry out a need or promise
to satisfy a requirement

normalIntro.en: Satisfy works for people, needs, rules, and doubts alike.

normal.en: The answer did not satisfy the teacher.
normal.cn: 这个答案没能让老师满意。

normal.en: He ate bread to satisfy his hunger.

abstract.en: Picture a cup filled exactly to the right level.

abstract.en: Imagine a lock clicking shut on the last number.

abstract.en: Think of doubt melting once proof arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象证据到来后疑问随之消融。

examples.en: The meal satisfied our appetite.

examples.en: Candidates must satisfy the language requirement.

definition_en: finely chopped meat packed into a thin casing

sceneCN: 这里 sausage 是「香肠」（第 1 个义项）；句意：两根香肠正在锅里煎着。

senses.title: Meat in a casing
senses.definition: finely chopped meat packed into a thin casing
senses.definitionCN: 切碎后灌入细肠衣的肉
senses.example: They grilled sausages for lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 他们午餐烤了香肠。
senses.why: The core sense is chopped meat shaped by a casing.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是用肠衣定型的碎肉。

senses.title: Processed sausage product

senses.definitionCN: 做成香肠形状出售的加工肉制品

senses.exampleCN: 他买了一包香肠零食。

senses.title: Sausage shape

intro.en: Sausage traces from Latin salsus through Late Latin salsicia and Old French.
intro.cn: sausage 经晚期拉丁语 salsicia 和古法语，追溯到拉丁语 salsus。

items.en: Salsus means salted.
items.cn: salsus 意为盐腌的。

items.en: Salsicia named salted meat preparations.
items.cn: salsicia 指盐腌的肉类食品。

items.en: Saussiche named a seasoned meat casing.
items.cn: saussiche 指调味肉肠。

items.en: Sausige appeared for minced meat in a skin.
items.cn: sausige 指灌在肠衣中的碎肉。

items.en: Sausage covers fresh, cured, and industrial products.

note.en: Sausage is compared with look-alike words and other meat products.

entries.definition: a flavoured liquid for food

an aromatic herb
a sausage served in a long bun
a cured sausage sliced thin
a spicy cured sausage

normalIntro.en: Sausage can be remembered by its salt root and its shape.

definition_en: the size or extent of something, a set of marks for measuring, or a thin plate on a fish
core_image: 地图角落的一小段比例尺，标注着图上距离与现实距离的关系
scene: 地图下方标着比例尺。A scale is printed at the bottom of the map.
sceneCN: 这里 scale 是「刻度；比例尺」（第 2 个义项）；句意：地图底部印着比例尺。

senses.title: Size and extent
senses.definition: the size or extent of something, especially when large
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的规模或范围，尤指较大规模
senses.example: The project was built on a huge scale.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目以巨大的规模建成。
senses.why: The core abstract sense is how far something reaches.
senses.whyCN: 核心抽象义是事物所达到的范围。

senses.title: Measuring marks
senses.definition: a set of marks or numbers used for measuring
senses.definitionCN: 用于测量的一组刻度或数字
senses.example: Read the weight on the scale.
senses.exampleCN: 读出秤上的重量。
senses.why: A ladder of marks turns size into a readable measure.
senses.whyCN: 一串刻度把大小转化为可读的度量。

senses.title: Fish plate
senses.definition: one of the thin hard plates covering a fish or reptile
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖鱼或爬行动物身体的薄硬片
senses.example: The fish's scales shone in the light.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼鳞在光下闪闪发亮。
senses.why: The layered plates look like small measuring marks.
senses.whyCN: 层叠的薄片看起来像小刻度。

senses.title: Weighing device

senses.why: The balanced beam is marked like a measuring scale.

senses.title: Climb up
senses.definition: to climb up or over something steep
senses.definitionCN: 攀上或翻越陡峭之物
senses.example: They scaled the wall before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在黎明前翻过了墙。
senses.why: Climbing a ladder resembles moving up a scale.
senses.whyCN: 爬梯子就像沿着刻度向上移动。

senses.title: Resize proportionally

senses.definitionCN: 在保持比例的情况下改变某物的大小

senses.exampleCN: 把图片缩放到适合页面。

abstract.cn: 攀登与测量共享台阶的意象。

examples.en: The company expanded on an international scale.
examples.cn: 这家公司以国际规模扩张。

examples.en: The map has a scale of one to fifty thousand.
examples.cn: 这张地图的比例尺是一比五万。

examples.en: Workers scaled the cliff to reach the cave.
examples.cn: 工人们攀上悬崖到达洞穴。

dict_mnemonic.text: scale 源自「梯子」，梯子的台阶就是刻度；由此引申出规模、比例尺、音阶、鱼鳞和攀登。

root: 源自拉丁语 scala（梯子、台阶），核心义「一级一级的量度」，由此扩展到规模、刻度、比例与攀登。

sensesIntro.en: Scale means size, measuring marks, fish plates, a weighing device, climbing, or resizing.
sensesIntro.cn: scale 意为规模、刻度、鱼鳞、天平、攀登，或按比例缩放。

core.en: A ladder-like set of steps used to measure or climb.
core.cn: 像梯子一样用于度量或攀爬的一级级台阶。

branches.en: Measured size becomes the idea of scale.
branches.cn: 被度量的大小成为规模概念。

branches.en: The marks themselves form a measuring scale.
branches.cn: 刻度本身构成测量标尺。

branches.en: Overlapping plates resemble tiny steps.
branches.cn: 层叠的鳞片像微小的台阶。

branches.en: The weighing beam is marked like a scale.
branches.cn: 天平横梁像刻度尺一样被标记。

branches.en: Climbing up and scaling an image both follow a ratio.
branches.cn: 向上攀登与缩放图像都遵循某种比率。

intro.en: Scale has a productive family in measurement and technology.
intro.cn: scale 在度量与技术领域有能产的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin scala, a ladder, is the source of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scala（梯子）是整个词族的来源。

items.meaning: a weighing device or fish plates
the act of climbing or resizing
items.example: Scaling the wall took an hour.

items.meaning: able to grow or be resized

items.example: They tested the scalability of the app.
items.exampleCN: 他们测试了应用的可扩展性。

items.meaning: a device or program that resizes

items.example: They plan to scale up production.
We must scale down the design.
items.exampleCN: 我们必须缩小设计规模。

definition_en: to pass a device over something, to look through quickly, or to examine closely
core_image: 一束光在纸面上来回移动，把文字变成电脑里的图像
scene: 医生把片子放进机器里扫描。The doctor scanned the image for problems.
sceneCN: 这里 scan 是「扫描」（第 1 个义项）；句意：医生扫描图像查找问题。

senses.title: Use a scanning device
senses.definition: to pass a machine or beam over something to read or record it
senses.definitionCN: 让机器或光束掠过某物以读取或记录
senses.example: Please scan the barcode at the till.
senses.exampleCN: 请在收银台扫描条形码。
senses.why: The core sense is a moving beam that captures a surface.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是移动的光束捕捉一个表面。

senses.title: Look through quickly
senses.definition: to read or look through something quickly
senses.definitionCN: 快速阅读或查看某物
senses.example: I scanned the menu and chose soup.
senses.exampleCN: 我浏览菜单，选了汤。
senses.why: The eye sweeps the page like a scanning beam.
senses.whyCN: 目光像扫描光束一样掠过页面。

senses.title: Examine closely
senses.definition: to examine something carefully in search of details
senses.definitionCN: 仔细检查某物以寻找细节
senses.example: He scanned her face for a sign.
senses.exampleCN: 他审视她的脸寻找迹象。
senses.why: A slow scan searches every part of the surface.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢扫描会探查表面的每个部分。

senses.title: Mark verse metre
senses.definition: to mark the stressed and unstressed beats of a poem
senses.definitionCN: 标出诗句中的重读与非重读音步
senses.example: Students scanned the lines of Latin verse.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们标出拉丁诗句的格律。
senses.why: The old sense is climbing through a line beat by beat.
senses.whyCN: 古老义项是逐拍走过一行诗。

senses.title: Medical image
senses.definition: a medical test that produces an image of the inside of the body
senses.definitionCN: 生成身体内部图像的医学检查
senses.example: The scan showed a small fracture.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示有一处小骨折。
senses.why: The device action becomes the name of the test.
senses.whyCN: 设备动作转化为检查的名称。

intro.en: Scan comes from Latin scandere, to climb, which also meant to scan verse.
intro.cn: scan 源自拉丁语 scandere（攀登），也指逐拍分析诗句。

items.en: Scandere means to climb or mount.
items.cn: scandere 意为攀登、上升。

items.en: Scansion named the marking of verse rhythm.
items.cn: scansion 指标记诗句节奏。

items.en: Scanning verse meant moving through each foot.
items.cn: 分析诗句意味着逐个音步走过。

items.en: Scanen meant to examine verse closely.
items.cn: scanen 意为仔细分析诗句。

items.en: The word extended to beams and medical imaging.
items.cn: 该词扩展到光束与医学成像。

note.en: Scan is compared with similar spellings and with other ways of looking.
note.cn: 把 scan 与形近词以及其它观看方式作比较。

entries.definition: very little or barely enough
a dishonest plan for money
a mark left by a wound
to read quickly for the main idea
to look at something closely
to move quickly over an area

normalIntro.en: Scan joins the idea of climbing through verse with sweeping a beam over a surface.
normalIntro.cn: scan 把逐拍走过诗句与光束扫过表面联系起来。

normal.en: A scanner sweeps a line of light across the page.
normal.cn: 扫描仪让一条光扫过页面。

normal.en: To scan a menu is to sweep your eyes down it fast.
normal.cn: scan 菜单就是目光快速向下扫过。

normal.en: The double n appears in scanned and scanning.
normal.cn: scanned 和 scanning 中都有双写 n。

normal.en: A brain scan is a picture made by scanning.
normal.cn: 脑部扫描是由扫描生成的图像。

normal.en: Scan the crowd means searching faces quickly.
normal.cn: scan the crowd 意为快速搜寻人脸。

abstract.en: Scanning turns a surface into information.
abstract.cn: 扫描把一个表面转化为信息。

abstract.en: Fast looking finds the shape; slow scanning finds the detail.
abstract.cn: 快速浏览找到轮廓，缓慢扫描找到细节。

abstract.en: The beam and the eye both move in lines.
abstract.cn: 光束和目光都以线条移动。

examples.en: She scanned the receipt into the computer.
examples.cn: 她把收据扫描进电脑。

examples.en: He scanned the report for any mention of cost.
examples.cn: 他快速浏览报告寻找有关成本的提及。

examples.en: The guard scanned the crowd at the gate.
examples.cn: 警卫在门口扫视人群。

dict_mnemonic.text: scan 原指「一步步攀登」诗句的格律，后来引申为光束一行行扫过，即扫描；再引申为目光快速浏览。

root: 源自拉丁语 scandere（攀登），经「逐拍分析诗行」引申为扫视、扫描，核心义「一行行地掠过」。

sensesIntro.en: Scan means to use a beam or machine, to look through quickly, to examine closely, or a medical image.
sensesIntro.cn: scan 意为用光束或机器扫描、快速浏览、仔细审视，或医学扫描检查。

core.en: To move steadily across a surface, as a beam or an eye.
core.cn: 像光束或目光一样稳定地掠过表面。

branches.en: A device sweeps and records a surface.
branches.cn: 设备掠过并记录表面。

branches.en: The eye sweeps text for key points.
branches.cn: 目光掠过文字抓取要点。

branches.en: The eye moves slowly to catch details.
branches.cn: 目光缓慢移动以捕捉细节。

branches.en: The old sense of walking through verse beats.
branches.cn: 逐拍走过诗句的古老义项。

branches.en: The action of scanning produces a medical scan.
branches.cn: 扫描动作产生了医学扫描检查。

intro.en: Scan has a small but active family in technology and poetry.
intro.cn: scan 在技术与诗歌领域有一个小而活跃的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb scandere, to climb, is the distant source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 scandere（攀登）是远源。

items.meaning: to sweep over or a medical test

latinEntries.meaning: a climbing or scanning of verse

definition_en: an action or event that causes public shock and disapproval
core_image: 报纸头版印着醒目的标题，路人停下脚步议论纷纷
scene: 报纸头版爆出公司财务丑闻。The newspaper revealed a financial scandal.
sceneCN: 这里 scandal 是「丑闻」（第 1 个义项）；句意：报纸揭露了一起财务丑闻。

senses.title: Public disgrace
senses.definition: an action or event that causes public shock and disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 引起公众震惊与谴责的行为或事件
senses.example: The minister resigned over a corruption scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 部长因腐败丑闻辞职。
senses.why: The core sense is a public shock that damages reputation.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是损害名誉的公共震惊事件。

senses.title: Malicious gossip
senses.definition: talk that spreads shocking or unkind stories about people
senses.definitionCN: 传播关于他人的惊人或不友善故事的闲话
senses.example: The village was full of scandal about the new neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 村里到处都是关于新邻居的流言。
senses.why: The shock of an event feeds the talk that spreads it.
senses.whyCN: 事件的震惊滋养了传播它的闲话。

senses.title: Moral outrage
senses.definition: a feeling of shock and moral disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 震惊与道德上的不赞同之感
senses.example: Their behaviour caused scandal among the older guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的行为在年长宾客中引起反感。
senses.why: The event produces the emotion it is named for.
senses.whyCN: 事件产生了以之命名的情绪。

intro.en: Scandal comes from Greek skandalon, a trap or stumbling block, through Latin.
intro.cn: scandal 经拉丁语源自希腊语 skandalon，意为陷阱或绊脚石。

items.en: Skandalon means a snare or a cause of stumbling.
items.cn: skandalon 意为圈套或使人跌倒的原因。

items.en: Scandalum meant a stumbling block or offence.
items.cn: scandalum 意为绊脚石或冒犯。

items.en: Scandale carried the sense of public disgrace.
items.cn: scandale 带有公开耻辱之义。

items.en: Scandal named shameful conduct and gossip.
items.cn: scandal 指可耻行为与流言。

items.en: Scandal covers politics, business, and celebrity life.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scandal 涵盖政治、商业与名人生活。

note.en: Scandal is compared with similar spellings and with words for shame and gossip.
note.cn: 把 scandal 与形近词以及表示耻辱和流言的词作比较。

entries.definition: an open shoe with straps
to burn with hot liquid
to look over quickly
loss of honour and respect
a strong feeling of shock and anger
talk about other people's private lives

normalIntro.en: Scandal can be remembered through its sense of a public stumble.
normalIntro.cn: 可以通过「当众跌倒」的意思记住 scandal。

normal.en: A scandal is a public stumble that everyone sees.
normal.cn: 丑闻是所有人都看见的当众失足。

normal.en: The word has scan at the beginning and dal at the end.
normal.cn: 这个词开头是 scan，结尾是 dal。

normal.en: A corruption scandal often ends a career.
normal.cn: 腐败丑闻常常终结一个人的职业生涯。

normal.en: Scandalous describes behaviour that shocks people.
normal.cn: scandalous 形容令人震惊的行为。

normal.en: A scandal sheet is a paper full of gossip.
normal.cn: scandal sheet 是充满八卦的小报。

abstract.en: A scandal is a private failure made public.
abstract.cn: 丑闻是被公开的私人失败。

abstract.en: Gossip spreads a scandal faster than facts can.
abstract.cn: 流言传播丑闻比事实更快。

abstract.en: The word once meant a trap, and a scandal still catches people.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指陷阱，而丑闻至今仍会让人中招。

examples.en: The scandal damaged the company's reputation.
examples.cn: 这起丑闻损害了公司的声誉。

examples.en: Reporters kept the scandal alive for weeks.
examples.cn: 记者们让这桩丑闻持续发酵了数周。

examples.en: She refused to take part in the gossip and scandal.
examples.cn: 她拒绝参与那些流言蜚语。

dict_mnemonic.text: scandal 原指「绊倒人的陷阱」，一个人当众跌倒就成丑闻；可记「当众失足，满城风雨」。

root: 源自希腊语 skandalon（陷阱、绊脚石），经拉丁语 scandalum 入英语，核心义「使人跌倒、招致公愤的事」。

sensesIntro.en: Scandal means a shocking public event, the gossip around it, or the outrage it causes.
sensesIntro.cn: scandal 意为令人震惊的公开事件、围绕它的流言，或它引起的愤慨。

core.en: A public shock caused by shameful behaviour.
core.cn: 可耻行为引起的公众震惊。

branches.en: The core event that shocks the public.
branches.cn: 震惊公众的核心事件。

branches.en: Talk that spreads the shocking story.
branches.cn: 传播惊人故事的闲话。

branches.en: The moral outrage felt by observers.
branches.cn: 旁观者感到的道德愤慨。

branches.en: An event and the gossip about it feed each other.
branches.cn: 事件与关于它的流言相互助长。

branches.en: A shameful event produces public outrage.
branches.cn: 可耻事件引发公众愤慨。

intro.en: Scandal has a family of adjectives, verbs, and compounds.
intro.cn: scandal 有形容词、动词和复合词构成的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin scandalum, a stumbling block, is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scandalum（绊脚石）是直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 这番话让观众大为震惊。
散布丑闻的人毁了她的名声。

items.example: He never reads a scandal sheet.

items.exampleCN: 受丑闻打击的银行失去了客户。

definition_en: not available in large enough amounts; difficult to find
core_image: 干旱的土地上，水桶里只剩下浅浅一层水
scene: 旱季里，干净的水变得稀缺。Clean water is scarce during the dry season.
sceneCN: 这里 scarce 是「稀缺的；不足的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：旱季里干净的水很稀缺。

senses.title: Not enough in amount
senses.definition: existing in amounts too small for what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 数量太少，不足以满足需要
senses.example: Food was scarce after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后食物短缺。
senses.why: The core sense is a short supply of something needed.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是所需之物供应不足。

senses.title: Rare to find
senses.definition: uncommon and hard to find
senses.definitionCN: 不常见且难以找到
senses.example: Such birds are scarce in this region.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鸟在这一带很罕见。
senses.why: A limited supply makes a thing uncommon.
senses.whyCN: 有限的供应使某物变得少见。

senses.title: In short supply
senses.definition: difficult to obtain because demand is higher than supply
senses.definitionCN: 因需求高于供应而难以获得
senses.example: Housing is scarce in the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 市中心住房供不应求。
senses.why: Economic shortage is the social form of scarcity.
senses.whyCN: 经济短缺是稀缺的社会形态。

intro.en: Scarce comes from Old French scars, from Latin excarpsus, plucked out.
intro.cn: scarce 源自法语古语 scars，更早来自拉丁语 excarpsus（被摘除的）。

items.en: Excarpsus means plucked out or selected.
items.cn: excarpsus 意为被摘除或被挑出的。

items.en: Excerpere means to pick out or to take away.
items.cn: excerpere 意为挑出或拿走。

items.en: Scars meant sparing, limited, or hard to get.
items.cn: scars 意为节省的、有限的、难得的。

items.en: Scarce named a short supply of goods.
items.cn: scarce 指货物供应不足。

items.en: Scarce is central to economics and ecology.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scarce 是经济学与生态学的核心词。

note.en: Scarce is compared with similar spellings and with words for shortage.
note.cn: 把 scarce 与形近词以及表示短缺的词作比较。

entries.definition: to frighten someone
a cloth worn around the neck
a mark left by a wound
not common
not enough for a purpose
thinly spread or scattered

normalIntro.en: Scarce and scarcity share a picture of empty shelves.
normalIntro.cn: scarce 与 scarcity 共享空货架的画面。

normal.en: A scarce item is like a shelf almost empty.
normal.cn: 稀缺的东西就像几乎空了的货架。

normal.en: Scarce adds ce to scar, but the sound is different.
normal.cn: scarce 比 scar 多了 ce，但读音不同。

normal.en: Scarcity is the noun from scarce.
normal.cn: scarcity 是 scarce 的名词形式。

normal.en: Scarce resources are a basic idea in economics.
normal.cn: 稀缺资源是经济学的基本概念。

normal.en: Clean water becomes scarce in a dry season.
normal.cn: 旱季里干净的水会变得稀缺。

abstract.en: Scarcity forces people to choose.
abstract.cn: 稀缺迫使人们做出选择。

abstract.en: What is scarce often becomes precious.
abstract.cn: 稀缺之物常常变得珍贵。

abstract.en: A full world still has scarce clean air.
abstract.cn: 即使世界很满，干净空气仍然稀缺。

examples.en: Jobs are scarce in the small town.
examples.cn: 这个小镇的工作机会很少。

examples.en: Water grew scarce as the summer went on.
examples.cn: 随着夏天推移，水变得稀缺。

examples.en: The government must decide how to share scarce resources.
examples.cn: 政府必须决定如何分配稀缺资源。

dict_mnemonic.text: scarce 与 scarcity 同族，可联想「空空的货架」：需要的东西不够，就是 scarce。

root: 源自拉丁语 excarpsus（被摘出的），经古法语 scars 进入英语，核心义「被取走大半、所剩无几」。

sensesIntro.en: Scarce means not enough, hard to find, or in short supply.
sensesIntro.cn: scarce 意为数量不足、难以找到，或供不应求。

core.en: A supply that is too small for the need.
core.cn: 相对于需求而言过于稀少的供应。

branches.en: The core state of not having enough.
branches.cn: 数量不足的核心状态。

branches.en: Rarity makes a thing hard to find.
branches.cn: 稀有使某物难以找到。

branches.en: Demand outruns supply in the market.
branches.cn: 市场中需求超过供应。

branches.en: Too little of something makes it uncommon.
branches.cn: 某物太少就会变得不常见。

branches.en: Rarity and high demand create shortage.
branches.cn: 稀有与高需求共同造成短缺。

intro.en: Scarce forms nouns and adverbs about shortage.
intro.cn: scarce 构成表示短缺的名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin excerpere, to pick out, is the distant root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 excerpere（挑出）是远源。

items.example: The scarceness of rain worried farmers.
Clean water is the scarcest resource.
items.exampleCN: 干净的水是最稀缺的资源。
我们必须保护稀缺资源。

definition_zh: 短缺；稀缺；稀少；资源不足以满足需求的状态
definition_en: the state in which something needed exists in a quantity too small to satisfy the demand for it
core_image: 集市收摊时只剩最后一筐苹果，围上来的人却比开市时更多
scene: 集市收摊后，最后一筐苹果前反而围了更多人，摊主悄悄翻过价格牌。Scarcity pushed the price of the last basket higher than the first.
sceneCN: 这里 scarcity 指「物品稀少而需求仍在，因而产生溢价的情形」（第 9 个义项：因稀少而形成的附加价值）；句意为稀缺把最后一筐的价格抬得比第一筐还高。图中可辨识物件：空摊位、最后一筐苹果、围拢的人群、翻面的价牌。

pos.zh: 短缺；稀缺；稀少（可数指具体的一次短缺，不可数指普遍状态）

senses.title: A shortage of something needed
senses.definition: the condition in which the supply of a needed thing is smaller than the amount people require
senses.definitionCN: 所需之物的供给小于人们所需数量的状况
senses.example: Scarcity of clean water shaped the town's history.
senses.exampleCN: 洁净水的短缺塑造了这座小镇的历史。
senses.why: Scarcity names a relationship, not a count: the same amount can be plentiful in one place and scarce in another because demand differs.
senses.whyCN: scarcity 命名的是关系而非数量：同样的量在一处充裕、在另一处稀缺，因为需求不同。

senses.title: Limited means against unlimited wants
senses.titleCN: 经济学：有限资源面对无限欲望
senses.definition: the founding condition of economics, in which resources are finite while human wants are not
senses.definitionCN: 经济学的出发点：资源有限而人的欲望无限
senses.example: Economics begins with scarcity and asks how to allocate.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学从稀缺出发，追问如何分配。
senses.why: Political economy took the everyday word and made it the reason markets and choices exist at all.
senses.whyCN: 政治经济学把这个日常词提升为市场与选择之所以存在的理由。

senses.title: The rarity of a particular object
senses.definition: the quality of being hard to find or obtain, as of a rare book or a scarce stamp
senses.definitionCN: 难以找到或取得的性质，如稀见书或罕邮票
senses.example: The scarcity of the first edition made it expensive.
senses.exampleCN: 初版书的稀有使它昂贵。
senses.why: Collectors use the word for the object itself, because what matters is how few survive rather than how many are wanted.
senses.whyCN: 收藏者用这个词指物本身，因为要紧的是存世多少，而不是多少人想要。

senses.title: Resource depletion in ecology
senses.definition: the falling availability of a natural resource as it is used up or its habitat shrinks
senses.definitionCN: 自然资源因被耗尽或栖息地缩小而日益不可得
senses.example: Scarcity of nesting sites reduced the colony.
senses.exampleCN: 营巢地的稀缺使这个群落变小。
senses.why: Ecology views scarcity as a limit that shapes behaviour, competition and population size.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把稀缺看作塑造行为、竞争与种群规模的限制。

senses.title: Perceived scarcity and the mindset it creates
senses.titleCN: 感知到的稀缺及其心态
senses.definition: a felt shortage that narrows attention, encourages hoarding and pushes people toward short-term choices
senses.definitionCN: 感到的短缺，它会收窄注意力、促使人囤积并偏向短期选择
senses.example: A scarcity mindset kept the team from sharing information.
senses.exampleCN: 稀缺心态让这个团队不愿共享信息。
senses.why: Psychology separated the state from the perception, because people act on what they believe is scarce.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把状态与感知分开，因为人是按自己所相信的稀缺去行动的。

senses.title: Not enough hours in the day
senses.definition: the shortage of time relative to the tasks and commitments one has accepted
senses.definitionCN: 相对于已接受的任务与承诺而言的时间不足
senses.example: Time scarcity, not money, kept her from finishing the course.
senses.exampleCN: 让她没能修完课程的，是时间稀缺而非缺钱。
senses.why: The word extends easily to time, because hours are a fixed supply that cannot be increased by effort.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很容易延伸到时上，因为小时是固定供给，再努力也加不出来。

senses.title: Attention and information scarcity
senses.definition: the shortage of attention available for a flood of information, or of reliable information itself
senses.definitionCN: 面对信息洪流时注意力的不足，或可靠信息本身的不足
senses.example: Information scarcity was replaced by information overload.
senses.exampleCN: 信息稀缺已被信息过载取代。
senses.why: Media economics applied the word to attention, since the scarce thing in an abundant market is the audience's focus.
senses.whyCN: 传媒经济学把这个词用到注意力上，因为在充裕的市场里，稀缺的是受众的专注。

senses.title: Artificial scarcity created on purpose
senses.titleCN: 为获利而人为制造的稀缺
senses.definition: a shortage deliberately maintained by a seller, cartel or platform to keep prices or status high
senses.definitionCN: 卖方、卡特尔或平台为维持高价或地位而有意保持的短缺
senses.example: The limited release was artificial scarcity, not a real shortfall.
senses.exampleCN: 限量发售是人为稀缺，并非真的缺货。
senses.why: Once scarcity can be manufactured, the word no longer assumes a natural limit; it can describe a strategy.
senses.whyCN: 一旦稀缺可以被制造，这个词就不再假定自然极限，而可以指一种策略。

senses.title: The premium that rarity adds to value
senses.titleCN: 因稀少而产生的价值溢价
senses.definition: the extra price or prestige an item gains because few like it are available
senses.definitionCN: 物品因同类稀少而获得的额外价格或声望
senses.example: Scarcity pushed the price of the last basket higher than the first.
senses.exampleCN: 稀缺把最后一筐的价格抬得比第一筐还高。
senses.why: Value can come from the supply side alone: when the same thing is abundant it is cheap, and when it is nearly gone it is dear.
senses.whyCN: 价值可以只来自供给一侧：同样的东西多时便宜，快没有时就贵。

intro.en: Scarcity came into English from Old French in the fourteenth century, but its deeper root is disputed between two accounts that are still taught side by side. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: scarcity 在十四世纪经古法语进入英语，但其更深词源在两种说法之间至今仍有争议，两种说法常并列讲授。年代均为约数。

items.en: One account derives scarcitas from parcus 'sparing, frugal'. The deeper origin of parcus is uncertain; the suggestion that it comes from parcere 'to spare' is a hypothesis rather than a proved link.
items.cn: 一种说法把 scarcitas 追溯到 parcus「节省的、俭省的」。parcus 的更深来源不确定；认为它出自 parcere「节省」的说法是假说，而非已证实的联系。

items.en: Scarcitas meant 'scarcity, scantiness'. On this account the noun passed into Old French as scarcete and then into English.
items.cn: scarcitas 意为「短缺、稀少」。按这一说法，该名词进入古法语作 scarcete，再进入英语。

items.en: Old French scarcete meant 'smallness, scantiness, stinginess' and English scarcity first carried that sense of meagre supply before widening to any shortage.
items.cn: 古法语 scarcete 意为「少、不足、吝啬」，英语 scarcity 最初带这种「供给寒酸」的意思，后扩为任何短缺。

items.en: The competing account connects the adjective scarce to Vulgar Latin excarpsus 'plucked out', from ex- 'out' plus carpere 'to pluck'. This account explains the adjective but does not settle the noun.
items.cn: 对立说法把形容词 scarce 连到俗拉丁 excarpsus「被摘出的」，出自 ex-「向外」加 carpere「摘取」。这一说法解释了形容词，却未能定下名词的来源。

items.en: From the nineteenth century classical economics made scarcity the central condition of economic life, and the word acquired its technical sense of finite means against unlimited wants.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，古典经济学把稀缺定为经济生活的核心条件，这个词于是获得「有限手段面对无限欲望」的技术义。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): the derivation is disputed between parcus and excarpsus, and no single earliest citation is fixed for the modern economic sense, so its first date is approximate; any older Indo-European forms offered for this family are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：词源在 parcus 与 excarpsus 之间存疑，现代经济义也没有公认的最早书证，首见年代只能约计；凡为这个词族给出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that look close to scarcity but differ in part of speech, meaning or root; group two holds other nouns of not having enough, each with a different reason for the shortfall.
note.cn: 第一组是与 scarcity 形近、但词性、含义或词根不同的词；第二组是其他表示「不够」的名词，每一个的短缺原因都不同。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'hard to obtain in quantity'; scarcity is the noun built on it in meaning, even where the derivation is debated.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「数量稀少、难以取得」；scarcity 在语义上是它的名词形式，尽管词源仍有争议。

entries.definition: Means 'barely, hardly', not 'sparsely'; the adverb has drifted away from the idea of quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「几乎不、勉强」，而非「稀少地」；这个副词已偏离数量概念。

entries.definition: Thinly spread, from Latin sparsus 'scattered'; it looks close to scarce but shares no root with it.
entries.definitionCN: 分布稀疏的，出自拉丁 sparsus「散开的」；与 scarce 外形相近，但并无共同词根。

entries.definition: A rarer synonym of scarcity formed with -ness; it names the state without the economic overtones.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -ness 构成的较罕用同义词；它只指状态，不带经济学色彩。

entries.definition: A plain word for a supply that is below the amount required, usually temporary or local.
entries.definitionCN: 指供给低于所需数量的普通词，通常是临时或局部的。

entries.definition: An old word for a scarce supply, especially of food; it comes from dear in the sense of costly, not from scarcity.
entries.definitionCN: 指供给稀少、尤指食物的旧词；它出自表示「昂贵」的 dear，而非出自 scarcity。

entries.definition: A formal noun for a small number or amount, from Latin paucus 'few'; it stresses fewness rather than unmet demand.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指数量很少，出自拉丁 paucus「少」；它强调数量少，而非需求未被满足。

entries.definition: The quality of being uncommon; a rare thing may be plentiful in absolute terms and still be uncommon in kind.
entries.definitionCN: 不常见的性质；稀见之物在绝对数量上可能很多，只是在种类上少见。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Scarcity is the noun of scarce; the -ity ending turns the adjective into a state.
normal.cn: scarcity 是 scarce 的名词，-ity 后缀把形容词变成状态。

normal.en: The economic sense is fixed in one phrase: limited resources against unlimited wants.
normal.cn: 经济义固定在一句话里：有限资源面对无限欲望。

normal.en: The family runs scarce, scarcely, scarceness, scarcity and water-scarce.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 scarce、scarcely、scarceness、scarcity 与 water-scarce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: water scarcity, food scarcity, resource scarcity, artificial scarcity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：水资源短缺、粮食短缺、资源稀缺、人为稀缺。

normal.en: Sparse looks like scarce but comes from sparsus 'scattered', so the two are false relatives.
normal.cn: sparse 看起来像 scarce，却出自 sparsus「散开的」，两者是假同源。

abstract.en: Picture the last basket on a table and every hand reaching at once.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上最后一筐，所有手同时伸过去。

abstract.en: Picture a day with more tasks than hours, so each choice costs another choice.
abstract.cn: 想象一天里任务多过小时，每个选择都要用另一个选择来换。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf kept almost empty on purpose so that the few items look precious.
abstract.cn: 想象货架故意留得几乎空着，好让剩下的几件显得珍贵。

examples.en: Classical economics treats scarcity as the reason choice is necessary.
examples.cn: 古典经济学把稀缺视为选择之所以必要的原因。

examples.en: The scarcity of rare earths reshaped the electronics supply chain.
examples.cn: 稀土资源的稀缺重塑了电子产业供应链。

examples.en: Artificial scarcity can keep a price high long after demand has fallen.
examples.cn: 人为稀缺可以在需求下降很久之后仍把价格维持在高位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「scarce（稀少）+ ity」——东西少、要的人多 → 稀缺、短缺

root: 古法语 scarcete < 拉丁 scarcitas「短缺」；词根一说为 parcus「俭省的」，另一说与俗拉丁 excarpsus「摘出的」（ex- + carpere）相关，两说并存未定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one relation: a supply is smaller than the demand on it. The word then becomes the foundation of economics, the state of a rare object, an ecological limit, a mindset, a shortage of time, of attention, a shortage made on purpose and finally a premium on price.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个关系展开：供给小于对它的需求。这个词随后成为经济学的基础、稀见物的状态、生态的限制、一种心态、时间与注意力的不足、有意制造的不足，最后是价格上的溢价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one last basket on an emptying table while more hands reach for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：空下去的桌上只剩最后一筐，伸过来的手却更多。

branches.en: THE GAP: the everyday shortfall and the founding condition of economics are the same relation formalised.
branches.cn: 缺口：日常的不足与经济学的出发点，是同一关系被形式化。

branches.en: FEWNESS: a rare object and a depleted habitat are both cases of supply falling.
branches.cn: 稀少：稀见之物与枯竭的栖息地，都是供给下降的情形。

branches.en: MIND: perception can produce the behaviour of scarcity before the shortage arrives.
branches.cn: 心态：感知可以在短缺到来之前就制造出稀缺的行为。

branches.en: NON-MATERIAL: hours and attention are fixed or finite supplies of their own.
branches.cn: 非实物：小时与注意力本身就是固定或有限的供给。

branches.en: MADE AND PRICED: scarcity can be staged, and rarity can be charged for.
branches.cn: 制造与定价：稀缺可以被安排出来，稀少也可以被收费。

intro.en: Scarcity is a noun formed with a Latin state suffix on a stem whose own origin is disputed, so the suffix is certain while the root is not.
intro.cn: scarcity 是用拉丁状态后缀构成的名称，词干本身的来源有争议，因此后缀确定而词根不确定。

latinIntro.en: The state suffix -itas gives English -ity in scarcity, rarity and paucity; the root is variously traced to parcus 'sparing' or to excarpsus 'plucked out'.
latinIntro.cn: 状态后缀 -itas 在 scarcity、rarity 与 paucity 中作英语 -ity；词根则有 parcus「俭省的」与 excarpsus「摘出的」两种追溯。

items.exampleCN: 旱情之后洁净水很稀缺。

items.exampleCN: scarceness 是 scarcity 更朴素的双胞胎。

items.exampleCN: 稀缺定价压低了高峰需求。

definition_en: to make someone feel afraid, or to become afraid
core_image: 半夜一声怪响，孩子们猛地缩进被子里
scene: 半夜的怪声把孩子们吓坏了。A strange noise scared the children at midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 scare 是「惊吓」（第 1 个义项）；句意：半夜的怪声吓坏了孩子们。

senses.title: Frighten someone
senses.definition: to make a person or animal feel afraid
senses.definitionCN: 使人或动物感到害怕
senses.example: The loud bang scared the dog.
senses.exampleCN: 巨响吓到了狗。
senses.why: The core sense is causing sudden fear.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是引起突然的恐惧。

senses.title: Become frightened
senses.definition: to become afraid, especially of a sudden danger
senses.definitionCN: 尤指面对突然危险时变得害怕
senses.example: The horse scares easily at loud sounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这匹马容易被大声响吓到。
senses.why: The same action can be felt from the inside.
senses.whyCN: 同一动作也可以从受惊者内部来感受。

senses.title: Sudden alarm
senses.definition: a sudden feeling or period of public fear
senses.definitionCN: 突然的恐惧感或公众恐慌期
senses.example: The food scare led to empty shelves.
senses.exampleCN: 食品恐慌导致货架空荡。
senses.why: The verb becomes the name of the fear it creates.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为它所造成的恐惧的名称。

intro.en: Scare comes from Old Norse skjarr, timid, and entered English in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: scare 源自古诺尔斯语 skjarr（胆怯的），于中世纪进入英语。

items.en: Skjarr meant timid or easily frightened.
items.cn: skjarr 意为胆怯的、易受惊的。

items.en: Skerren meant to frighten or drive away.
items.cn: skerren 意为使害怕或驱赶。

items.en: Scare became the common verb for sudden fear.
items.cn: scare 成为表示突然恐惧的常用动词。

items.en: Scarecrow and scare tactics entered common use.
items.cn: scarecrow 与 scare tactics 进入常用语。

items.en: Scare also names public alarms such as health scares.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scare 也指健康恐慌等公众警报。

note.en: Scare is compared with similar spellings and with other fear verbs.
note.cn: 把 scare 与形近词以及其它表示恐惧的动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Scare is one letter away from scar, and both come from harm.
normalIntro.cn: scare 与 scar 只差一个字母，都与伤害有关。

normal.en: A scare can leave a scar on the memory.
normal.cn: 一次惊吓可能在记忆里留下疤痕。

normal.en: Scared is the adjective for feeling fear.
normal.cn: scared 是表示感到害怕的形容词。

normal.en: A scarecrow scares birds away from crops.
normal.cn: 稻草人把鸟从庄稼旁吓走。

normal.en: Scare away and scare off both mean drive off.
normal.cn: scare away 与 scare off 都表示吓退。

normal.en: A health scare is a sudden public worry about illness.
normal.cn: health scare 是关于疾病的突然公众担忧。

abstract.en: Fear arrives in a second but can last for years.
abstract.cn: 恐惧一秒钟到来，却可能持续多年。

abstract.en: A scare tests whether we can still think clearly.
abstract.cn: 惊吓检验我们是否还能清醒思考。

abstract.en: The same word names the act and the alarm.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指吓人的动作，也指惊慌。

examples.en: Don't scare me like that again.
examples.cn: 别再那样吓我了。

examples.en: The dog scared the birds out of the garden.
examples.cn: 狗把鸟吓出了花园。

examples.en: The city recovered after the food scare.
examples.cn: 食品恐慌过后，城市恢复了平静。

dict_mnemonic.text: scare 与 scar 形近，可记「被吓（scare）得留下疤（scar）」，核心是突然使人害怕。

root: 源自古诺尔斯语 skjarr（胆怯的），经中古英语 skerren 进入英语，核心义「使人突然害怕」。

sensesIntro.en: Scare means to frighten someone, to become frightened, or a sudden alarm.
sensesIntro.cn: scare 意为吓唬某人、受惊害怕，或突然的恐慌。

core.en: Sudden fear caused by a threat.
core.cn: 由威胁引起的突然恐惧。

branches.en: Causing fear in another person or animal.
branches.cn: 使他人或动物产生恐惧。

branches.en: Being startled and feeling afraid.
branches.cn: 受到惊吓并感到害怕。

branches.en: A period of fear shared by many people.
branches.cn: 许多人共同经历的恐慌期。

branches.en: The giver and receiver of fear share one verb.
branches.cn: 施加恐惧者与承受恐惧者共用一个动词。

branches.en: A threat can scare one person or a whole city.
branches.cn: 一个威胁可以吓到一个人或整座城市。

intro.en: Scare builds a family of adjectives, tools, and tactics.
intro.cn: scare 构成形容词、工具和策略等词族。

latinIntro.en: Scare is Germanic, from Old Norse, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: scare 源自日耳曼语族中的古诺尔斯语，因此不列拉丁词根。

items.example: She was scared of the dark.

items.example: A scarecrow stood in the field.

definition_en: a cloth worn around the neck, or to eat something very quickly
core_image: 雪天里一条羊毛围巾绕在脖子上，一端垂到胸前
scene: 雪天里一条羊毛围巾绕在脖子上，一端垂到胸前。She wrapped a scarf around her neck.
sceneCN: 这里 scarf 是「围巾」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她把围巾绕在脖子上。

senses.title: A cloth worn around the neck
senses.definition: A cloth worn around the neck
senses.definitionCN: 绕在脖子上的布
senses.example: She wrapped a scarf around her neck.
senses.exampleCN: 她把围巾绕在脖子上。
senses.why: Scarf came from a French word for a sash, a band worn across a soldier's shoulder, then narrowed to the cloth for the neck.
senses.whyCN: scarf 源自法语中表示绶带的词，本指士兵斜挎的带子，后专指围在颈上的布。

senses.title: To eat something very quickly
senses.definition: To eat something very quickly
senses.definitionCN: 很快地吃完
senses.example: He scarfed the sandwich in a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他一分钟就把三明治吞了下去。
senses.why: The old slang sense of scarf, to eat greedily, grew from the image of a mouth wrapped and then filled.
senses.whyCN: scarf 俚语中表示贪吃的旧义，来自把嘴裹住再塞满的画面。

intro.en: The history of scarf is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: scarf 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: The word first named a band.
items.cn: 这个词最初指一条带子。

items.en: Soldiers wore it as a sash.
items.cn: 士兵把它斜挎在肩上。

items.en: The band narrowed to a scarf.
items.cn: 带子收窄成了围巾。

items.en: Slang turned it into eating.
items.cn: 俚语又把它变成吃。

items.en: Scarf covers cloth and eating.

definition_en: to throw things over an area or to make a group move apart
core_image: 一阵风把桌上的纸页吹得漫天飞舞，四处落下
scene: 风把桌上的纸张吹得四散。The wind scattered the papers across the desk.

senses.title: Throw over an area
senses.definition: to throw small things over a surface or area
senses.definitionCN: 把小东西抛撒在一个表面或区域上
senses.example: She scattered seeds across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她把种子撒遍田地。
senses.why: The concrete sense is distributing small objects widely.
senses.whyCN: 具体义是把小物件广泛分布。

senses.title: Drive a group apart
senses.definition: to make a group of people or animals move in different directions
senses.definitionCN: 使一群人或动物朝不同方向散开
senses.example: The police scattered the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 警察驱散了人群。
senses.why: Objects spreading apart become people driven apart.
senses.whyCN: 物件四散引申为人被驱散。

senses.title: Break up and spread
senses.definition: to separate and move in different directions
senses.definitionCN: 分开并朝不同方向移动
senses.example: The birds scattered when the cat appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 猫一出现，鸟群就散开了。
senses.why: The group itself can do the scattering.
senses.whyCN: 群体自身也可以执行散开的动作。

senses.title: Spread out data
senses.definition: to spread points or values over an area in statistics
senses.definitionCN: 在统计中把点或数值分散到某个区域
senses.example: The graph shows how the data scatter.
senses.exampleCN: 图表显示了数据如何分散。
senses.why: The visual spread of points is called scatter.
senses.whyCN: 点的视觉分布被称为散点。
