definition_zh: 食腐动物；拾荒者；清除剂
definition_en: an animal or person that feeds on what others have left behind, especially dead matter
core_image: 一只秃鹫落在尸体旁，把别人不要的剩肉吃干净
scene: 这里指「食腐动物」。 Vultures act as scavengers, stripping a carcass before disease can spread.
sceneCN: 这里 scavenger 是「食腐动物」（第 1 个义项：以动物尸体为食的动物）；句意：秃鹫充当食腐动物，在疾病扩散之前把尸体清理干净。

pos.zh: 食腐动物；拾荒者；清道夫；清除剂（可数，复数 scavengers）

derivatives.zh: 寻宝游戏（收集物品的活动）

senses.title: An animal that eats carrion
senses.definition: an animal that feeds on the dead bodies or remains of other animals
senses.definitionCN: 以其他动物尸体或残骸为食的动物
senses.example: Wolves often work as scavengers in winter, feeding on kills they did not make.
senses.exampleCN: 狼在冬季常充当食腐者，取食并非自己捕杀的猎物。
senses.why: The word labels an animal by what it takes from others' leftovers, so the diet is defined by the source rather than the species.
senses.whyCN: 这个词按「从别人剩余物中取食」来给动物分类，因此食性由食物来源定义，而不是由物种定义。

senses.title: A large carrion bird
senses.definition: specifically, a bird such as a vulture or a crow that locates and consumes carcasses
senses.definitionCN: 特指秃鹫、乌鸦等能发现并取食尸体的鸟类
senses.example: The vulture's bare head is an adaptation of a dedicated scavenger.
senses.exampleCN: 秃鹫裸露的头是专职食腐者的一种适应。
senses.why: Large birds are the most visible scavengers, so the general noun often points to them without further qualification.
senses.whyCN: 大型鸟类是最显眼的食腐者，因此这个普通名词常常不加限定就指向它们。

senses.title: A person who picks through waste
senses.definition: a person who collects usable material from discarded waste
senses.definitionCN: 从废弃物品中收集可用材料的人
senses.example: Scavengers sorted bottles and metal from the landfill edge.
senses.exampleCN: 拾荒者在垃圾填埋场边缘分拣瓶子和金属。
senses.why: Human waste-picking repeats the animal pattern of living on what others discard, so the same word moved from carcasses to rubbish.
senses.whyCN: 人类拾荒重复了动物「靠别人丢弃物生活」的模式，于是同一个词从尸体移到了垃圾。

senses.title: A street cleaner
senses.definition: historically, a worker or vehicle employed to clean streets and remove refuse
senses.definitionCN: 历史上受雇清扫街道、清运垃圾的工人或车辆
senses.example: The medieval scavenger was a paid official, not a beggar.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的 scavenger 是有薪的官吏，而不是乞丐。
senses.why: The word's oldest English sense is institutional, naming the officer who kept streets clear; the animal sense came later.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在英语中最古老的意思是制度性的，指负责保持街道清洁的官员；动物义项出现得更晚。

senses.title: A cleaner of the ecosystem
senses.definition: an organism whose feeding removes dead organic matter and recycles its nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 通过取食清除死亡有机物并回收养分的生物
senses.example: Beetles and flies are the small scavengers that clear the forest floor.
senses.exampleCN: 甲虫和蝇类是清理森林地表的小型食腐者。
senses.why: Ecology reframes the eater as a service: consuming dead matter is how nutrients return to the system.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把取食者重新描述为一项服务：吃掉死去的物质，正是养分回到系统的方式。

senses.title: A chemical remover
senses.definition: a substance that removes unwanted molecules, such as free radicals or impurities
senses.definitionCN: 除去不需要的分子（如自由基或杂质）的物质
senses.example: Vitamin C serves as a scavenger of free radicals in the cell.
senses.exampleCN: 维生素 C 在细胞中充当自由基清除剂。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the image of something sweeping leftovers away, and the target became reactive molecules instead of meat.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了「把剩余物扫走」的形象，被清扫的对象从肉变成了活性分子。

senses.title: An industrial clean-up device
senses.definition: equipment or a process that removes waste gases or residues from a stream
senses.definitionCN: 从气流或液流中除去废气或残渣的设备或工艺
senses.example: The scrubber works as a scavenger for sulphur compounds in the exhaust.
senses.exampleCN: 洗涤器充当废气中硫化合物的清除装置。
senses.why: Industry applies the same removal idea to flows of gas and liquid, so the word can name a machine as well as a substance.
senses.whyCN: 工业把同样的「清除」思路用到气液流动上，因此这个词既能指物质，也能指设备。

senses.title: One who lives off leftovers
senses.titleCN: 靠他人剩余物生活的人
senses.definition: figuratively, a person who takes advantage of what others leave unused or abandoned
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指利用他人未用或弃置之物的人
senses.example: Critics called the middlemen scavengers of the industry's failed projects.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把这些中间商称为该行业失败项目的拾荒者。
senses.why: The literal image of feeding on remains supplies a moral metaphor for opportunism, without changing the core relation.
senses.whyCN: 「以残余为食」的字面形象为机会主义提供了一种道德隐喻，而核心关系并未改变。

intro.en: Scavenger began as a customs and street officer, then slid into the animal that cleans up carcasses.
intro.cn: scavenger 起初指海关与街道官吏，后来滑向「清理尸体的动物」这一义项。

items.en: The word traces to Anglo-French scawage, a toll or charge on goods, and scawager, the officer who collected it and inspected streets. The ultimate source is usually taken to be a Frankish verb meaning 'to look at', reconstructed as skauwon; that form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 这个词上溯至盎格鲁-法语 scawage「货物税」与 scawager「收税并巡查街道的官吏」。其最终来源一般认为是一个表示「看」的法兰克语动词，重构形式作 skauwon；这一形式属于重构，并非有记录的词。

items.en: English adopted scavager in the sixteenth century. The ending was later remodeled to -enger, as in messenger, producing scavenger.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 scavager。词尾后来被改造成 -enger（如 messenger），于是产生了 scavenger。

items.en: For centuries a scavenger was a paid official who kept streets clear of refuse, a sense still recorded in historical writing.
items.cn: 在数百年间，scavenger 指受雇保持街道无垃圾的官吏，这一义项在历史写作中仍有记录。

items.en: The ecological sense, an animal living on carrion, becomes common in the nineteenth century with the rise of natural history writing. The exact first use is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 指以腐肉为生的动物这一生态义项，随 19 世纪博物学写作的兴起而常见。确切首见年代尚无定论。

items.en: Twentieth-century chemistry extended scavenger to substances that remove free radicals or impurities, and industry to clean-up devices.
items.cn: 20 世纪的化学把这个词扩展到除去自由基或杂质的物质，工业界则扩展到净化装置。

note.en: The first group shares the root; the second holds other feeders and cleaners.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一词根；第二组是其他取食者与清理者。

entries.definition: The action of feeding on remains or searching waste; scavenger is the one that does it.
entries.definitionCN: 指食腐或翻找废弃物的动作；scavenger 指实施这一动作的生物。

entries.definition: Names the activity or describes it; it never names the animal itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指这项活动或作定语描述，不能直接指动物本身。

entries.definition: Describes what has been picked over, as in scavenged bone; it marks the object, not the eater.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已被翻找过的对象，如被啃食过的骨头；它标记的是对象，不是取食者。

entries.definition: An animal that eats detritus, mostly dead plant fragments; scavenger usually points to animal carcasses.
entries.definitionCN: 以腐屑（多为死亡植物碎片）为食的动物；scavenger 通常指取食动物尸体。

entries.definition: A bacterium or fungus that breaks matter down chemically; a scavenger eats and digests, a decomposer mineralizes.
entries.definitionCN: 通过化学方式分解物质的细菌或真菌；食腐者取食消化，分解者则把物质矿化。

entries.definition: An animal that hunts live prey; a scavenger takes what is already dead.
entries.definitionCN: 捕杀活猎物的动物；食腐者取食已经死去的动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real relatives, real phrases and the historical street sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实同族词、真实搭配与历史上的街道义项。

normal.en: The verb is scavenge; the activity is scavenging; the actor is scavenger.
normal.cn: 动词是 scavenge，活动是 scavenging，施行者是 scavenger。

normal.en: The word began as a street officer, which explains why it can still mean a cleaner.
normal.cn: 这个词最初指街道官吏，这也解释了它为何仍可表示「清扫者」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases reveal the range: carrion scavenger, scavenger hunt, free-radical scavenger.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出词义范围：食腐尸动物、寻宝游戏、自由基清除剂。

normal.en: A vulture on a carcass is the default picture of the word.
normal.cn: 秃鹫立在尸体旁，是这个词最典型的画面。

normal.en: The -enger ending also appears in messenger and harbinger, all old agent nouns.
normal.cn: -enger 词尾也出现在 messenger 与 harbinger 中，都是古老的施动名词。

abstract.en: Think of a city's night crew: nobody produces the rubbish, but someone must clear it.
abstract.cn: 想象城市的夜班工人：垃圾不是他们制造的，但总得有人清走。

abstract.en: A scavenger is a recycling plant that walks.
abstract.cn: 食腐者就是一座会走路的回收厂。

abstract.en: In chemistry the same word is a sweeper that removes what the reaction does not want.
abstract.cn: 在化学里，同一个词是清扫工，专门清走反应不想要的东西。

examples.en: Scavengers such as jackals can move nutrients across a whole valley.
examples.cn: 像豺这样的食腐动物能把养分搬运到整片山谷。

examples.en: The antioxidant acts as a scavenger of damaging radicals.
examples.cn: 这种抗氧化剂充当有害自由基的清除剂。

examples.en: City records show that a scavenger was paid to clear the market square.
examples.cn: 城市档案显示，曾有一位清扫官吏受雇清理集市广场。

dict_mnemonic.text: scav（谐音「死尸」）+ enger → 处理死尸的人 → 食腐动物、拾荒者

root: 盎格鲁-法语 scawager「收税并巡查街道的官吏」，来自 scawage「货物税」；其更早来源一般认为是一个表示「看」的法兰克语动词（重构形式 *skauwōn），属于重构而非确证词形。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: living on what others leave. The eater may be an animal, a person, a chemical or a machine, but the relation stays the same.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个想法展开：靠别人留下的东西生活。取食者可以是动物、人、化学物质或机器，但那个关系始终不变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a consumer that lives on remains others abandon.
core.cn: 核心意象：靠他人弃置的残余为生的取食者。

branches.en: THE CORE: dead bodies supply the food, and large birds make the pattern most visible.
branches.cn: 核心：尸体提供食物，大型鸟类让这一模式最显眼。

branches.en: HUMAN WASTE: people who pick through rubbish repeat the animal relation, while the oldest sense is the paid street officer.
branches.cn: 人类废弃物：翻拣垃圾的人重复了动物的关系，而最古老义项则是受薪的街道官吏。

branches.en: THE SERVICE: ecology reads carrion eating as nutrient recycling, not as theft.
branches.cn: 服务：生态学把食腐读作养分循环，而不是「偷食」。

branches.en: THE MOLECULE: chemistry retargets the sweeping action from flesh to radicals and impurities.
branches.cn: 分子：化学把清扫动作的对象从肉体改成自由基与杂质。

branches.en: MACHINE AND METAPHOR: industry builds devices that scavenge exhaust, and critics use the word for opportunists.
branches.cn: 机器与隐喻：工业造出清除废气的装置，批评者则用这个词指机会主义者。

intro.en: Scavenger is an old agent noun whose ending was reshaped by English speakers; its parts are no longer transparent.
intro.cn: scavenger 是一个古老的施动名词，词尾经英语使用者改造，其构件已不再透明。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved. The base is Anglo-French scawage, with a Germanic source usually reconstructed as Frankish skauwon; the English -enger ending is by analogy with messenger.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词不涉及拉丁词根。词基是盎格鲁-法语 scawage，其日耳曼语来源一般重构为法兰克语 skauwon；英语词尾 -enger 是类比 messenger 改造而来。

items.example: The beetle is a scavenger of the forest floor.
items.exampleCN: 这种甲虫是森林地表的食腐者。

items.meaning: to feed on remains or search waste
items.example: Rats scavenge around the bins at night.
items.exampleCN: 老鼠夜间在垃圾桶周围觅食。

items.meaning: the activity of living on remains
items.example: Scavenging by gulls increases near landfills.
items.exampleCN: 垃圾填埋场附近海鸥的拾食活动会增加。

items.meaning: picked over or removed as waste
items.meaningCN: 被翻拣过的；作为废弃物被清除的
items.example: The scavenged carcass was reduced to bones.
items.exampleCN: 被啃食过的尸体只剩下骨头。

items.example: Messenger and scavenger share the reshaped ending.
items.exampleCN: messenger 与 scavenger 共享这个被改造的词尾。

items.meaning: one that announces what is coming
items.example: The first frost is a harbinger of winter.
items.exampleCN: 初霜是冬天将至的预兆。

items.example: Carrion attracts a crowd of scavengers.
items.exampleCN: 腐肉招来一群食腐动物。

items.example: The street officer removed refuse each morning.
items.exampleCN: 街道官吏每天早晨清走垃圾。

definition_zh: 情景；设想；剧情提纲；剧本大纲；方案
definition_en: a described sequence of possible events, a sketch of a plot, or a projected situation used for planning
core_image: 舞台后方那顶棚屋与布景板：剧情被一幕一幕写在一块板上
scene: 这里指「情景」。 In a darkened theatre, the director sketches the opening scenario on a board while the actors wait behind the stage wall.
sceneCN: 这里 scenario 是「戏剧剧情提纲」（第 5 个义项：分幕写下的剧情概要）；句意：在昏暗的剧场里，导演在板子上勾出开场剧情提纲，演员们在舞台墙后等候。图中可辨识物件：布景板、导演的笔、剧本、幕布、后台的演员。

pos.zh: 情景；设想；可能发生的一系列事件
剧情提纲；剧本大纲；（规划的）方案

derivatives.zh: 风景的；舞台布景的（同 scaena 词根）

senses.title: Imagined sequence: a possible chain of events
senses.titleCN: 设想的事件序列：可能发生的一串事
senses.definition: a described or imagined series of events that could happen
senses.definitionCN: 被描述或想象出来、可能发生的一连串事件
senses.example: We outlined three scenarios for the coming year.
senses.exampleCN: 我们为来年勾画了三种情景。
senses.why: Italian scenario first meant a sketch of a play's scenes. An imagined future is written the same way: a sequence of scenes laid out on a board before anything happens.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 scenario 最初指一部戏各场次的提纲。想象的未来也用同样的方式写：事情发生前，一串场景先被排在板上。

senses.title: Screenplay outline: the film's scenes on paper
senses.titleCN: 电影剧本大纲：纸上的各场戏
senses.definition: a written outline of the scenes and action of a film or television programme
senses.definitionCN: 电影或电视节目各场次与情节的书面概要
senses.example: The director rejected the first scenario as too slow.
senses.exampleCN: 导演否决了第一版剧本大纲，认为它太拖沓。
senses.why: This is the Italian sense carried into film: before dialogue, there is a list of scenes. The scenario is the skeleton of the story, not yet the flesh of the script.
senses.whyCN: 这是意大利语含义进入电影后的用法：在对白之前，先有一份场次清单。scenario 是故事的骨架，还不是剧本的血肉。

senses.title: Worst-case scenario: the scene you fear
senses.titleCN: 最坏情况：你最怕的那一幕
senses.definition: in the phrase worst-case scenario, the most unfavourable outcome that could reasonably happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于 worst-case scenario，指在合理范围内可能发生的最不利结果
senses.example: In the worst-case scenario, the whole plant would shut down.
senses.exampleCN: 最坏的情况下，整座工厂会停工。
senses.why: A scenario is a scene you can rehearse in the mind. The worst case is the darkest scene in that rehearsal, written out so that it can be prepared for instead of merely feared.
senses.whyCN: scenario 是可以在脑中预演的一幕。worst case 就是这场预演里最暗的一幕，把它写出来，才能做准备，而不只是害怕。

senses.title: Scenario planning: rehearsing several futures
senses.titleCN: 情景规划：预演几种未来
senses.definition: a planning method in which an organization works out several possible futures and prepares for each
senses.definitionCN: 组织推演若干种可能未来并为每一种做准备的方法
senses.example: Scenario planning helped the company survive the oil shock.
senses.exampleCN: 情景规划帮助公司挺过了石油危机。
senses.why: The stage image becomes a method: several scenes are written instead of one script, and the planner keeps all of them ready because no single scene is guaranteed.
senses.whyCN: 舞台意象变成一种方法：不是写一个剧本，而是写好几幕，规划者把每一幕都准备好，因为没有哪一幕是被保证的。

senses.title: Dramatic scenario: the outline of the plot
senses.titleCN: 戏剧剧情提纲：情节的概要
senses.definition: the original sense: a brief outline of the scenes and plot of an opera, play or ballet
senses.definitionCN: 最初的含义：歌剧、戏剧或芭蕾各场次与情节的简要提纲
senses.example: The opera's scenario was printed in the programme.
senses.exampleCN: 这部歌剧的剧情提纲印在节目单上。
senses.why: The Italian word was born in the opera house: scenario is the scene-by-scene plan from which the libretto and music were built.
senses.whyCN: 这个意大利词诞生于歌剧院：scenario 是逐场的计划，剧本与音乐都从它搭建起来。

senses.title: Climate scenario: a projected physical future
senses.titleCN: 气候情景：被推演出的物理未来
senses.definition: a scientifically modelled set of future climate conditions based on stated assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 基于明确假设、由科学模型推演的一套未来气候条件
senses.example: The high-emission climate scenario predicts a two-metre rise.
senses.exampleCN: 高排放气候情景预测海平面上升两米。
senses.why: The 'scene' is now drawn with data rather than words: a scenario is a coherent picture built from assumptions, so that its consequences can be examined.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“场景”用数据而不是文字画成：scenario 是由假设构建的一幅自洽图景，以便检查它的后果。

senses.title: Scenario analysis: comparing the scenes
senses.titleCN: 情景分析：把几幕放在一起比较
senses.definition: a method of comparing outcomes under different stated assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 在不同明确假设下比较结果的方法
senses.example: Scenario analysis showed that both plans carried similar risk.
senses.exampleCN: 情景分析显示两个方案承担的风险相近。
senses.why: The word shifts from a single scene to the act of lining scenes up side by side. Analysis is possible because each scenario is a closed, self-consistent picture.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从单独一幕转到把几幕并排摆放的动作。之所以能分析，是因为每个 scenario 都是一个封闭而自洽的图景。

senses.title: Best-case scenario: the brightest scene
senses.titleCN: 最好情况：最亮的那一幕
senses.definition: in the phrase best-case scenario, the most favourable outcome that could reasonably happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于 best-case scenario，指在合理范围内可能发生的最有利结果
senses.example: The best-case scenario still leaves us short of staff.
senses.exampleCN: 最好的情况仍然让我们缺人手。
senses.why: The same rehearsal, lit from the other side: the best case is the scene where every assumption goes right, written out to test whether even success would be enough.
senses.whyCN: 同一场预演，从另一侧打光：best case 是每个假设都顺利的那一幕，写出来是为了检验“即使成功是否也够”。

senses.title: Hypothetical situation: the scene you suppose
senses.titleCN: 假设情境：你设想出来的那一幕
senses.definition: a supposed situation used to explain a point, as in 'imagine a scenario where...'
senses.definitionCN: 为说明某个观点而设想的处境，如“设想这样一个情景……”
senses.example: Imagine a scenario in which the power fails during the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 设想手术过程中停电的情景。
senses.why: Here no future is predicted; a scene is simply staged in the imagination so that a rule or an argument can be tested inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这里并不预测未来，只是在想象中搭起一幕，让某条规则或某个论证能在这个场景里被检验。

intro.en: Scenario is an Italian theatre word, borrowed in the 19th century. Its Greek-Latin chain is well documented; only the later extensions are approximate in date.
intro.cn: scenario 是一个意大利语戏剧词，19 世纪被借入英语。它的希腊—拉丁链条有清楚记载；只有后来的引申年代是约略的。

items.en: First recorded in English in 1878, borrowed from Italian, for the outline of an opera's plot.
items.cn: 英语最早记录于 1878 年，借自意大利语，指歌剧情节的提纲。

items.en: Italian scenario meant 'scene, outline', built from scena 'scene' plus the suffix -ario.
items.cn: 意大利语 scenario 意为“场景、提纲”，由 scena“场景”加后缀 -ario 构成。

items.en: Italian scena goes back to Latin scaena 'stage, scene', the backdrop against which action was played.
items.cn: 意大利语 scena 可追溯到拉丁语 scaena“舞台、场景”，即动作表演所依靠的背景。

items.en: Latin scaena was borrowed from Greek skene, originally a tent or hut, then the wooden stage building behind the actors.
items.cn: 拉丁语 scaena 借自希腊语 skene，原指帐篷或棚屋，后来指演员身后那座木制舞台建筑。

items.en: The word spreads from opera to film and then to futures work: scenario planning and worst-case scenarios become standard in business and policy.
items.cn: 这个词从歌剧扩散到电影，再进入未来研究：情景规划与最坏情况在商业和政策中成为标准说法。

items.en: Modern English uses scenario for imagined futures, film outlines, climate projections and planning exercises. Scene, scenic and scenography share the same stage root.
items.cn: 现代英语用 scenario 指想象未来、电影大纲、气候推演与规划练习。scene、scenic、scenography 共享同一个“舞台”词根。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the stage root or a derived form; the near-meaning group compares what kind of imagined or written outline each word names.
note.cn: 形近组共享“舞台”词根或是派生形式；近义组比较每个词指的是哪一种想象或书面概要。

entries.definition: the painted backdrops of a stage, or the natural landscape of a place. It shares scaena 'stage' but means the visible setting, not the plot.
entries.definitionCN: 舞台的绘景，或某地的自然风景。它同出 scaena“舞台”，但指可见的布景，而不是情节。

entries.definition: a single division of a play, or a place where something happens. Scenario is the outline of several scenes; scene is one of them.
entries.definitionCN: 戏剧中的一个场次，或事件发生的地点。scenario 是若干场次的提纲，scene 是其中一场。

entries.definition: a person who writes scenarios or screenplays. It is scenario + -ist and not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 写剧本大纲或电影剧本的人。它是 scenario + -ist，不是独立词根词。

entries.definition: the set of circumstances existing at a particular time. It is usually actual, while a scenario is imagined or projected.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻实际存在的一组情况。它通常是现实的，而 scenario 是想象或推演出来的。

entries.definition: the connected events of a story. It is the finished chain of action, while a scenario is the outline written before it.
entries.definitionCN: 故事中相互关联的事件。它是完成的行动链，而 scenario 是它之前写下的提纲。

entries.definition: a short summary of the main points of something. It is general and can describe any plan, not only scenes.
entries.definitionCN: 某事要点的简短概括。它是通用词，可指任何计划，不限场景。

entries.definition: a particular instance or set of circumstances, as in worst case. It is more neutral and less narrative than scenario.
entries.definitionCN: 某个特定实例或一组情况，如 worst case。它比 scenario 更中性、叙事性更弱。

entries.definition: an estimate of a future value based on current data. It is numerical, while a scenario may be a whole qualitative story.
entries.definitionCN: 基于现有数据对未来数值的估计。它是数字化的，而 scenario 可以是完整的定性故事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Italian stage word and real planning phrases, not invented sound-alikes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的意大利语舞台词和真实规划短语，而不是编造的谐音。

normal.en: Italian scenario is scena 'scene' + -ario: literally 'a set of scenes'. That is why an outline and a future plan share the word.
normal.cn: 意大利语 scenario 是 scena“场景”+ -ario：字面就是“一组场景”。这就是提纲与未来计划共用这个词的原因。

normal.en: Greek skene was the hut behind the actors; Latin scaena was the stage; Italian scena was the scene. The whole chain is about what stands behind the action.
normal.cn: 希腊语 skene 是演员身后的棚屋；拉丁语 scaena 是舞台；意大利语 scena 是场景。整条链都关于“动作背后的那个东西”。

normal.en: Worst-case and best-case scenario are fixed phrases: the darkest and brightest scenes in the same mental rehearsal.
normal.cn: worst-case 与 best-case scenario 是固定短语：同一场脑内预演里最暗与最亮的两幕。

normal.en: Scenario planning writes several scripts instead of one, so that no single future can take the planner by surprise.
normal.cn: 情景规划写好几个剧本而不是一个，好让任何一种未来都不能让规划者措手不及。

normal.en: Climate scenario is the same stage image drawn with data: a coherent picture built from stated assumptions.
normal.cn: climate scenario 是用数据画出的同一舞台意象：由明确假设构建的一幅自洽图景。

abstract.en: Picture a board behind the stage with the scenes numbered on it. Before any actor speaks, the whole sequence already exists as a sketch.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台后方一块板，上面标着编号的场次。在任何演员开口之前，整个序列已经以草图的形式存在。

abstract.en: Move that board from the theatre to a meeting room, and the numbered scenes become possible futures; the sketch becomes a plan.
abstract.cn: 把这块板从剧场搬到会议室，编号的场次就变成可能的未来；草图就变成了方案。

abstract.en: A scenario is always a closed little world: it can be entered, compared with another and tested, which is why the word suits both plots and policy.
abstract.cn: scenario 永远是一个封闭的小世界：可以走进去、与另一个比较、被检验，所以这个词既适合情节，也适合政策。

examples.en: The report sets out three scenarios for the next decade.
examples.cn: 报告提出了未来十年的三种情景。

examples.en: In the worst-case scenario, the bridge would be closed for a year.
examples.cn: 最坏的情况下，这座桥会封闭一年。

examples.en: The film's scenario was rewritten four times before shooting.
examples.cn: 这部电影的剧本大纲在开拍前改了四次。

dict_mnemonic.text: “斯纳里欧”——斯纳里欧在台上演了一幕设想的戏 → scenario 情景、剧情提纲

root: 意大利语 scenario“场景、提纲”，来自 scena“场景”+ -ario；拉丁 scaena 源自希腊 skene“舞台、帐篷、棚屋”；核心是“把一串场景预先排在一块板上”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of scenario, all from one board of scenes: first a plot outline, then any imagined sequence, then a future that planners rehearse.
sensesIntro.cn: scenario 的九个义项都来自同一块“场次板”：先是剧情提纲，再是任何被想象的事件序列，最后是规划者预演的未来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board behind the stage on which the scenes of a story are numbered before they are performed.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台后方一块板，故事的各场次在表演之前就被编号排好。

branches.en: DRAMATIC OUTLINE: the opera scenario and the film scenario are the same written list of scenes before dialogue exists.
branches.cn: 戏剧提纲：歌剧 scenario 与电影 scenario 都是对白出现之前写好的场次清单。

branches.en: IMAGINED SEQUENCE: the numbered scenes become any supposed chain of events, whether predicted or merely used to test an argument.
branches.cn: 想象序列：编号的场次变成任何设想的事件链，无论是预测，还是仅用来检验论证。

branches.en: CASE EXTREMES: worst-case and best-case are the darkest and brightest scenes of the same mental rehearsal.
branches.cn: 情况两端：worst-case 与 best-case 是同一场脑内预演里最暗与最亮的两幕。

branches.en: PLANNING METHODS: scenario planning and scenario analysis compare several written futures side by side.
branches.cn: 规划方法：scenario planning 与 scenario analysis 把几个写好的未来并排比较。

branches.en: MODELLED FUTURE: a climate scenario draws the same scene with data, so its consequences can be examined.
branches.cn: 模型化未来：climate scenario 用数据画出同一场景，以便检查其后果。

intro.en: Scenario is an Italian borrowing, not an English prefixed word. English adds plural -s and builds compounds such as scenario-based and scenario planning.
intro.cn: scenario 是意大利语借词，不是英语加前缀构成的词。英语加复数 -s，并构成 scenario-based、scenario planning 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Latin scaena 'stage', from Greek skene 'tent, stage building'. English keeps scene, scenic, scenery and scenography from the same family, all pointing to what is visible on or behind a stage.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语 scaena“舞台”，来自希腊语 skene“帐篷、舞台建筑”。英语从同一家族保留 scene、scenic、scenery、scenography，都指向舞台上或舞台后可见的东西。

items.meaning: a set of scenes; an outline or projected situation
items.meaningCN: 一组场景；提纲或推演出的情境（scena + -ario）
items.example: The scenario describes a city without private cars.
items.exampleCN: 这个情景描述了一座没有私家车的城市。

items.meaningCN: 多个设想的情景（复数后缀）

items.meaning: a writer of scenarios or screenplays
items.meaningCN: 剧本作者；编剧（-ist 表示从事者）
items.example: The scenarist adapted the novel for the screen.
items.exampleCN: 编剧把这部小说改编成了电影。

items.meaningCN: 基于情景的（复合形容词）
items.example: The course uses a scenario-based approach.
items.exampleCN: 这门课程采用基于情景的方法。

items.meaning: the method of preparing for several possible futures
items.example: Scenario planning began in the oil industry.
items.exampleCN: 情景规划始于石油行业。

items.meaning: a division of a play, or a place of action
items.meaningCN: 戏剧场次；事件发生的地点（同 scaena 词根）
items.example: The last scene takes place in a hospital.
items.exampleCN: 最后一幕发生在一家医院里。

items.meaning: relating to scenery or a stage
items.meaningCN: 风景的；舞台布景的（-ic 表示“与……相关”）
items.example: The route is famous for its scenic views.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线以风景优美著称。

items.meaningCN: 舞台绘景；风景（-ery 构成集合名词）
items.example: The scenery changed at every act.

items.meaning: the art of designing stage sets
items.meaningCN: 舞台布景术；场景设计（-graphia 表示描绘）
items.example: Her scenography turned the stage into a forest.
items.exampleCN: 她的舞台设计把舞台变成了一片森林。

definition_en: the natural features of an area, or the painted sets on a stage
core_image: 火车窗外，青山与湖泊缓缓向后移动，像一幅展开的画卷
scene: 火车穿过山谷，窗外风景不断变换。The scenery outside the train kept changing.
sceneCN: 这里 scenery 是「风景」（第 1 个义项）；句意：火车外的风景不断变化。

senses.title: Natural landscape
senses.definition: the natural features of an area, such as hills, rivers, and forests
senses.definitionCN: 某地区的自然特征，如山丘、河流和森林
senses.example: We stopped to admire the scenery.
senses.exampleCN: 我们停下来欣赏风景。
senses.why: The core sense is the visible natural appearance of a place.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个地方可见的自然面貌。

senses.title: Stage sets
senses.definition: the painted boards and objects that represent a place on stage
senses.definitionCN: 舞台上用来表现地点的绘景板和道具
senses.example: The scenery was lowered between the acts.
senses.exampleCN: 幕间布景被放了下来。
senses.why: The theatre uses a built version of a natural view.
senses.whyCN: 剧场使用自然景色的搭建版本。

intro.en: Scenery is scene plus -ery, from Greek skene through Latin scaena.
intro.cn: scenery 由 scene 加 -ery 构成，经拉丁语 scaena 源自希腊语 skene。

items.en: Skene meant a stage building.
items.cn: skene 意为舞台建筑。

items.en: Scaena meant the stage.
items.cn: scaena 意为舞台。

items.en: Scenery named the painted stage background.
items.cn: scenery 指舞台上的绘景背景。

items.en: Romantic travel extended scenery to natural views.
items.cn: 浪漫主义旅行把 scenery 扩展到自然景色。

items.en: Scenery is mainly uncountable for natural landscape.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scenery 指自然风景时通常不可数。

note.en: Scenery is compared with similar spellings and with words for landscape.
note.cn: 把 scenery 与形近词以及表示风景的词作比较。

entries.definition: a place or unit of action

a burial ground
the visible features of an area

normalIntro.en: Scenery is the whole collection of scenes in a place.
normalIntro.cn: scenery 是一个地方所有场景的集合。

normal.en: Scene plus ery makes the mass noun scenery.
normal.cn: scene 加 ery 构成不可数名词 scenery。

normal.en: Scenery is uncountable, so we say beautiful scenery, not sceneries.
normal.cn: scenery 不可数，所以说 beautiful scenery，不说 sceneries。

normal.en: A change of scenery means a change of surroundings.
normal.cn: a change of scenery 意为换个环境。

normal.en: Stage scenery is the painted world behind the actors.
normal.cn: 舞台布景是演员身后的绘景世界。

normal.en: Mountain scenery is a common travel phrase.
normal.cn: mountain scenery 是常见的旅行说法。

abstract.en: Scenery is what the land looks like when no one is acting.
abstract.cn: 风景是大地在没有表演时的样子。

abstract.en: The same word frames both a valley and a stage.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既框住山谷也框住舞台。

abstract.en: Travel is often a search for new scenery.
abstract.cn: 旅行常常是在寻找新的风景。

examples.en: The scenery along the coast is spectacular.
examples.cn: 沿海的风景非常壮观。

examples.en: They moved to the countryside for a change of scenery.
examples.cn: 他们搬到乡下换个环境。

examples.en: The stage scenery showed a forest at night.
examples.cn: 舞台布景显示的是夜晚的森林。

dict_mnemonic.text: scenery 是 scene 加 -ery，指「场景的总和」；自然风景和舞台布景都用它，且不可数。

root: 由 scene 加 -ery 构成，scene 源自希腊语 skene（舞台建筑），核心义「一地的景色总观或舞台布景」。

sensesIntro.en: Scenery means the natural landscape of an area or the painted sets on a stage.
sensesIntro.cn: scenery 意为某地的自然风景，或舞台上的布景。

core.en: The visible appearance of a place or stage.
core.cn: 一个地方或舞台可见的面貌。

branches.en: The natural landscape people travel to see.
branches.cn: 人们旅行观赏的自然风景。

branches.en: The built background on a stage.
branches.cn: 舞台上搭建的背景。

branches.en: Both are framed views of a place.
branches.cn: 两者都是被框住的地方景象。

branches.en: Scenery can be found outdoors or built indoors.
branches.cn: 风景既可在户外发现，也可在室内搭建。

branches.en: Whether natural or painted, scenery sets the mood.
branches.cn: 无论天然还是绘制，风景都奠定氛围。

intro.en: Scenery belongs to the scene family of visual words.
intro.cn: scenery 属于 scene 的视觉词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin scaena, stage, is the source of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scaena（舞台）是该词族的来源。

items.exampleCN: 我们走了风景优美的路线。

items.meaning: a place or unit of action

items.example: The stage scenery was painted by hand.
items.exampleCN: 舞台布景是手工绘制的。

definition_en: a plan that lists times for events, or to arrange an event for a time
core_image: 秘书翻开日程本，把一个个会议填进格子里
scene: 秘书把会议加进了日程表。The secretary added the meeting to the schedule.
sceneCN: 这里 schedule 是「时间表」（第 1 个义项）；句意：秘书把会议加进了日程表。

senses.title: Timetable
senses.definition: a plan listing the times when events will happen
senses.definitionCN: 列出事件发生时间的计划
senses.example: My schedule is full this week.
senses.exampleCN: 我这周的日程排满了。
senses.why: The core sense is time laid out for events.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是为事件排布好的时间。

senses.title: Progress plan
senses.definition: a plan showing stages of work and when they should finish
senses.definitionCN: 显示工作阶段及其完成时间的计划
senses.example: The project is behind schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目落后于计划。
senses.why: A timetable for work becomes a progress plan.
senses.whyCN: 工作的时间表变成进度计划。

senses.title: Arrange a time
senses.definition: to arrange for something to happen at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 安排某事在特定时间发生
senses.example: They scheduled the interview for Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把面试安排在周一。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of putting events in time.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为把事件放入时间中的动作。

senses.title: Detailed list
senses.definition: a formal list of items, prices, or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 物品、价格或条件的正式清单
senses.example: The contract includes a schedule of costs.
senses.exampleCN: 合同包含一份费用清单。
senses.why: An ordered sheet lists what belongs where.
senses.whyCN: 有序的表格列出什么归在哪里。

intro.en: Schedule comes from Late Latin schedula, a small sheet of paper.
intro.cn: schedule 源自晚期拉丁语 schedula（小纸片）。

items.en: Skhida meant a leaf of papyrus or a strip.
items.cn: skhida 意为纸莎草叶或纸条。

items.en: Scheda meant a sheet of paper.
items.cn: scheda 意为一张纸。

items.en: Schedula was a small written note.
items.cn: schedula 是一张小便条。

items.en: Cedule named a written list or label.
items.cn: cedule 指书面清单或标签。

items.en: Schedule meant a note or explanatory list.
items.cn: schedule 意为便条或说明性清单。

items.en: Schedule now means a timetable or to arrange.
items.cn: 现代英语中 schedule 指时间表或安排。

note.en: Schedule is compared with similar spellings and with words for plans.
note.cn: 把 schedule 与形近词以及表示计划的词作比较。

entries.definition: a plan or a plot
an outline or model
education received at school
a list of times for events
a list of items for a meeting
an intended course of action

normalIntro.en: Schedule began as a small sheet of paper holding a list.
normalIntro.cn: schedule 最初指写有清单的一小张纸。

normal.en: A schedule is a sheet that tells you when things happen.
normal.cn: 时间表是一张告诉你何时做什么的纸。

normal.en: On schedule means exactly on time.
normal.cn: on schedule 意为准时。

normal.en: Behind schedule means late, ahead of schedule means early.
normal.cn: behind schedule 是落后，ahead of schedule 是提前。

normal.en: The British say shed-yool, Americans say sked-jool.
normal.cn: 英式读 shed-yool，美式读 sked-jool。

normal.en: A busy schedule leaves little free time.
normal.cn: 繁忙的日程几乎没有空闲时间。

abstract.en: A schedule turns time into a shape we can manage.
abstract.cn: 时间表把时间变成可以管理的形状。

abstract.en: Plans fail when the schedule is only a wish.
abstract.cn: 当时间表只是愿望时，计划就会失败。

abstract.en: A small sheet of paper can rule a whole day.
abstract.cn: 一张小纸片可以支配一整天。

examples.en: The train arrived on schedule.
examples.cn: 火车准时到达。

examples.en: He scheduled a call for the afternoon.
examples.cn: 他安排下午通电话。

examples.en: The building work is ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 建筑工程进度提前了。

dict_mnemonic.text: schedule 原指一张写有清单的小纸，后来指把时间排成清单，即日程表；动词即「安排」。

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 schedula（小纸片），经古法语 cedule 入英语，核心义「写有时间与事项的纸」。

sensesIntro.en: Schedule means a timetable, a progress plan, to arrange a time, or a detailed list.
sensesIntro.cn: schedule 意为时间表、进度表、安排时间，或明细清单。

core.en: A written sheet that orders events in time.
core.cn: 按时间排列事项的书面表格。

branches.en: The everyday timetable of events.
branches.cn: 日常事件的时间表。

branches.en: A plan for stages of work.
branches.cn: 工作阶段的计划。

branches.en: The act of setting a time.
branches.cn: 确定时间的动作。

branches.en: A formal list of items or costs.
branches.cn: 物品或费用的正式清单。

branches.en: The timetable and the act of arranging support each other.
branches.cn: 时间表与安排动作相互支撑。

intro.en: Schedule forms verbs and nouns about time management.
intro.cn: schedule 构成与时间管理有关的动词和名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin schedula, a small sheet, is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 schedula（小纸片）是直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 排日程是他的主要任务。
